**Bottom line:** SLV is falling on a macro move, not on anything specific to silver or the fund. The selling is a rates and dollar shock: hot October inflation, a Fed that is fully priced to hike in December, and a firm dollar. Nothing I found says the shock has ended. Silver's structural deficit story is intact but is not driving near-term price. The 1.6% after-hours bump has no identified catalyst.

**What is driving it**
- **Inflation and rate hikes**
  - October CPI was hot: headline +0.4% (0.3% expected), core +0.3% (0.2% expected). PPI was +6.5% year over year, the highest since November 2022 ([Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/why-is-silver-falling-dollar-treasury-yields-fed-rate-hike/cNb7QhcR9XJ), [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/silver-tumbles-over-3-as-fed-rate-hike-bets-fuel-us-dollar-rally-202611121711)).
  - A December hike is priced at roughly 95-100%, with about 10% odds of 50 basis points. FXStreet cites about 65% odds of another hike in January.
  - Hawks are lining up. Hammack said policy "needs to become restrictive", Waller floated 50 basis points, and Schmid said inflation is too hot. The Fed under Chair Warsh already hiked in September, to 3.75-4.00%.
  - The December meeting is December 8-9, per one undated preview.
- **Dollar and yields:** The dollar index was near 103.1, the highest since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury was above 5% (about 5.15% on November 16) and the 30-year about 5.47%. That is a heavy headwind for a non-yielding metal.
- **Equities:** Worries about the AI trade add to the risk-off tone. Gold broke below $3,800 on November 18 for the first time since September 2025.
- **Today's move:** Silver was down about 3% on November 18. Prices ranged from about $44.9 to $46.4, depending on source and time. Kitco showed about $44.94 late in the day. SLV's 41.34 after-hours print fits that, since the fund holds about 0.90 oz per share.
- **Trend:** Silver is down about 17% over a month and about 22% by Trading Economics' count. This is the lowest level since September 2025. I found no dedicated November 18 close wrap or after-hours explanation.

**Structural story (background, not a near-term driver)**
- Silver peaked near $121.6 on January 29, 2026, then fell about 50% by June on the hawkish Fed and a firm dollar ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/opinion/2026-06-25/silvers-squeeze-has-unwound-shortage-has-not)). The late-2025 squeeze has largely unwound: lease rates spiked to about 39%, and COMEX registered stocks have since rebuilt to roughly 87-100 million ounces.
- The Silver Institute and Metals Focus project a sixth straight annual deficit, 46.3 million ounces for 2026.
- Demand is weak: the Silver Institute sees 2026 demand down 5%, with industrial demand down 3% and jewelry hurt by high prices.
- Shanghai traded at a premium of about 10% or more to Western prices as of June. I found no November data on that.
- Trading Economics' model target is about $47 for year-end and about $39 in 12 months.

**Positioning and flows**
- **Positioning:** Kitco (October 28) says managed-money shorts bottomed below 5,000 contracts and have rebuilt to about 12,500. That is not an extreme. Another source showed a small net long as of October 27. The two disagree, and I found nothing newer than early November.
- **SLV holdings:** SLV held about 504.3 million ounces and about $25.2B of net assets on November 13, with about 558.65 million shares outstanding. Holdings were flat from November 11 to 13. The sources I found show mixed, undated flows, with no clear sign of capitulation.
- **Sentiment:** Retail sentiment on SLV turned "extremely bearish" (Stocktwits).

**Levels and catalysts**
- **Support:** I found no solid technical write-up. The only cited levels were a retail commenter's $44 and the round $50 that broke. The prior low of 42.01 on SLV is your own level. Silver was near its year-to-date low and oversold in late October too, and it kept falling.
- **Next catalyst:** Friday's PPI and more Fed commentary were named as upcoming catalysts.

**Reliability**
- The figures conflict across sources. Silver was quoted at about $47 and about $50 on the same days. SLV was called "down 31.5% year to date" while silver is described as up over the year.
- Several pages carry wrong or odd date stamps. The Trading Economics page showed November 19.
- Many sources are auto-generated or promotional.
- Treat exact levels with caution and use your own quote data.

**For a 1-10 session decision:** The oversold reading is real, but the cause is still intact, with a hike fully priced, hot inflation and a rising dollar. A bounce needs softer PPI, softer Fed talk or a dollar and yield pullback, and I found no sign of any of those yet. Silver fell through $50 with oversold RSI before and kept going. The after-hours pop is thin evidence of a turn.

agents.report:
**EC (Ecopetrol), research for 2026-11-18 after the close**

**Bottom line:** I found no news item that explains today's 5.3% drop. Brent fell only 1.3% today, so oil does not account for it. Today's price action looks like oil weakness plus a pile of Colombian fiscal and political overhangs, with some forced-selling feel. The company's own numbers are strong. Treat any bounce as a trade against heavy overhangs, not as a fix to the story.

**Today and the last few sessions**
- **Oil:** Brent settled at $91.95 (-1.3%). WTI settled at $83.26 (-3.2%), its lowest since Aug 26 (Reuters-based reports). EIA showed a 3.4M barrel US crude build against a 58k forecast.
- **Backdrop:** Brent is down about 20% month to date. It was in the $110s on Ecopetrol's own Q3 price basket (the basket averaged $110.3). The IEA expects a Q4 surplus and a "substantial" surplus in 2027. Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption is the only thing propping up the risk premium.
- **Prior closes:** 14.91 on Nov 16 (-3.4%) and about 14.86 on Nov 17. A 200-day average break was reported Nov 16.
- **Colombia (Nov 17):** The local COLCAP index fell 2.17% to 2,399. Rio Times could not pin a trigger. It cited a reported Q3 GDP of -0.8% quarter on quarter, but I could not verify that figure elsewhere. Treat it as unconfirmed.
- **Peso:** Steady near 3,317 per dollar.
- **Earlier slide:** The local share fell 3.2% on Nov 4 and 4.1-5.2% on Nov 5. Sirius, the Caribbean offshore gas project, slipped to 2031 (Reuters, Nov 5).
- **Range:** The 52-week range is $8.16 to $18.38. The stock was about $17.27 on Oct 5, so the 20-day drop is a full unwind of the October run.

**Fundamentals (Q3 results, released Nov 12 after a first-ever postponement)**
- **Earnings:**
  - Net income was COP 4.8 trillion, up 86%.
  - EBITDA was COP 15.9 trillion, a 45% margin.
  - Revenue was COP 35.1 trillion.
  - The refining margin was a record $45.6 per barrel.
- **Balance sheet:**
  - Debt is 2.1x EBITDA against a 2.5x ceiling.
  - Cash is COP 16.3 trillion.
  - It issued a $2B bond due 2034, rated BB by Fitch, to refinance the Brava acquisition loan.
- **Caveats:**
  - Profit rides oil and refining prices that are now rolling over.
  - Production is declining at mature fields, which management admitted.
  - Brava (Brazil, closed Aug 17 for $1.12B) is in the numbers for one month only.
  - The stock fell about 1.2% after the results, which analysts called in line.
- **Government owes it money:** The fuel price stabilisation fund (FEPC) owed COP 11.4 trillion. About COP 1.6 trillion of that dates from Q1 2025.
- **Guidance:** The Q3 call gave no 2027 guidance, capex or dividend figure. A 2027 investment plan and updated strategy are promised after board approval.

**Strategy and politics**
- **New government:** President Abelardo de la Espriella (elected June 2026) is pro-oil: reopen exploration, allow fracking, replace reserves. The stock rallied hard on his election, then fell about 8.5% the day after the runoff. Bank of America kept Underperform on the view that this was already priced in (a COP 1,900 target was cited, but the date is unclear).
- **New CEO:** Joaquín Gutiérrez started Sep 28. Press notes he has no hydrocarbons background and was a campaign manager for the president. Citi reportedly called his arrival a "missed opportunity", but I could not open that article.
- **Announced on the Nov 13 call:**
  - Restarting fracking in the Magdalena Medio (La Luna formation), though management said it is too early to size capex or production.
  - A 10-year gas purchase deal with Venezuela's PDVSA, with Ecopetrol operating the Colombian section of the Antonio Ricaurte pipeline.
  - A US OFAC (sanctions) license has been requested for the pipeline deal.
- **LNG:** It halted LNG import plans because LNG prices rose more than 196% year on year.
- **Analysts:** The MarketBeat consensus is Hold with a $15.95 average target (1 Strong Buy, 7 Hold, 1 Sell). Goldman is neutral at $17.70. Jefferies upgraded to Hold on Oct 29 with a $19 target, but that rests on a single aggregator source.

**Overhangs, which are the likely cause of the selling**
1. **Possible sale of a state stake.** The Centro Democrático party (the governing party, per La Nación) proposed selling about 8.5-9% of Ecopetrol under the "Ley de Rescate Fiscal". At market value that is roughly COP 9.7 trillion. The government has not formally proposed it. The USO oil union and the CUT labour federation are opposed, and the CUT has called a national strike for Nov 19. A sale would add supply and signal a state that needs cash.
2. **Fiscal rescue bill.** It reached Congress with a COP 51 trillion 2027 adjustment, and Congress has until Dec 16. **BILI research, as of the 2026-11-18 close.** I found no news that explains today's drop. The sell-off looks like analyst and positioning pressure, plus Tencent supply, ahead of earnings on Nov 24. Several sources conflict on small details, noted below.

**Thesis**
- Bilibili is a Chinese video and community platform with two engines. Advertising is growing fast and is now its largest revenue line. Mobile games are the weak spot and are expected to turn up in Q4.
- The stock is down about 46% year to date. It has gone from about $36 (52-week high) to about $11.5, with a 52-week low of $11.42. That is far below the analyst consensus target of about $28.79.
- The fall has been steady, not one event. Likely causes are a rating-downgrade wave, the Tencent selldown plus convertible dilution, a post-earnings fade, and weak China ADR sentiment.

**Fundamentals (Q2 2026, reported Aug 27)**
- Revenue rose 8% to RMB 7.94B. Net profit rose 55% to RMB 339M. Gross margin was 37.2%, the 16th straight quarter of year-over-year improvement. The company has about RMB 24.3B (about $3.58B) in cash and short-term investments.
- Advertising grew 28% to RMB 3.13B, the 14th straight quarter above 20%. Value-added services (memberships and similar) grew 5%.
- Mobile games fell 14% to RMB 1.39B. Management blamed the high base from last year's *San Guo: Mou Ding Tian Xia* (Three Kingdoms strategy game), which it now calls "stable and mature".
- Daily active users were 116.5M (+7%), monthly active users 371M, and time spent was 113 minutes. Paying users rose 7% to 33.4M.
- The company gave no numeric guidance. Medium-term targets are a 40-45% gross margin and a 15-20% operating margin. It had spent 70-80% of its RMB 1B AI capex target in the first half, with a RMB 500M hit to 2026 R&D.
- Management said the Q3 ad outlook is "confident", but cited a challenging macro environment. It expects games to return to year-over-year growth in Q4.
- Game pipeline:
  - Lumi Master (monster-catching RPG): global launch Sept 17.
  - BanG Dream! Our Notes: global launch Sept 24.
  - Second season of the NCard card game: October.
  - New licensed strategy game: Q4.
  - San Guo strategy game: toward the end of 2026.
  - The rest slip to 2027.
- I found no reporting on how the September launches are performing.

**Capital structure and Tencent**
- On Sept 4 the company priced $700M of convertible notes due 2031. Tencent took $200M of the notes and sold or was repurchased out of its Class Z shares (the ADS-backed ordinary shares). The stock fell about 18% over the following 30 days.
- Shareholders approved the Tencent repurchase on Oct 28. It closed Nov 5 at HK$115.38 per Class Z share (13.59M shares for $200M).
- Tencent's stake falls from about 3.3% to near zero. It would be about 2.3% if the notes were fully converted. So Tencent has largely exited its equity position, which fits an overhang story.
- Total shares fall from about 413M to about 400M after the repurchase. They rise to about 435M if the notes convert in full. I couldn't find the conversion price or coupon.
- A separate $300M two-year buyback was authorized in June. About $118M had been bought year to date as of the Q2 call. Management says it will keep buying "opportunistically".

**Recent price and analyst action**
- Nov 17: the stock fell 5.7% to $11.94. Nov 18: it fell another $0.38 (about 3.2%) to $11.56, on 2.15M shares against a 2.9M average.

**Earnings, Nov 24**

- That is two sessions after the Nov 20 close and inside your 1-10 session window. Nov 19-23 are the sessions before it.

The evidence against a fade is stronger than the evidence for one. I'd rate a short of the basket against XLRE as low conviction, leaning no trade or a very small one. **What the basket is doing right:**
- **Q3 reports are all in.** They ran from Oct 30 to Nov 5, and every name raised 2026 guidance. The following points are from secondary coverage and the 24/7 Wall St. summary.
  - **SPG** (Nov 5): Real Estate FFO was $3.37 against $3.22 a year ago, and 2026 guidance rose $0.10 to $13.30-$13.40. Mall and Outlets occupancy is 96.5%, the highest since 2016. The dividend went up to $2.30 a quarter. GAAP net income guidance was cut for the third quarter in a row, because of non-cash mark-to-market losses ($99.6M). Management said the next guidance comes in February 2027, and that holiday sales will decide how much SPG beats its target.
  - **KIM:** FFO was $0.47, up 6.8%, and leased occupancy hit a record 96.6%. It raised guidance and bought back $150M of stock. It also bought two Louisville centers for $295M on Nov 2. Its dividend is now $0.28 a quarter. About $466M of debt matures in 2027 at a 4% average coupon, so refinancing at today's rates costs some cash flow.
  - **REG:** Same-property NOI rose 5.1%, and the portfolio is a record 97.0% leased. Same-property NOI guidance rose to 4.25% or better. The dividend went up 6% to $0.80. A $65M non-cash impairment caused an EPS miss, and full-year GAAP EPS guidance fell to $2.31-$2.33. One source (Earnings Whispers, a single interpretation) says 2027 same-property NOI growth slows to the mid-3% range. That is the only real "peak growth" signal I found.
  - **FRT** (Oct 30): Core FFO was $1.87, up 5.6%. 2026 guidance rose to $7.54-$7.58. Cash leasing spreads were 14%, and small-shop leased occupancy was 94.1%. It bought back $95M of stock. Shares fell about 1% after the report.
  - **O** (Nov 2): AFFO per share was $1.12, and 2026 AFFO guidance rose to $4.45-$4.46. It kept its $10B investment target. The monthly dividend was raised to $0.2740 on Nov 10 (record date Nov 30, paid Dec 15). O is a net-lease REIT with a different profile from the shopping-center names, and it is the most rate-sensitive of the five.

It raised its 2027-28 EBITDA estimates by 7% but sees refining and marketing EBITDA falling about 48%. **Legal overhang**
- The Second Circuit reversed the $16.1B Petersen/Eton Park judgment against Argentina in March 2026 and vacated the order to turn over Argentina's YPF shares.
- Rehearing was reportedly denied, which would leave only the Supreme Court as an avenue, and the odds of review there are described as very low. I couldn't confirm the rehearing date. Burford is the plaintiff side ([Buenos Aires Herald](https://buenosairesherald.com/economics/ny-court-denies-burford-appeal-in-ypf-expropriation-case), [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1014413/burford-capital-statement-re-ypf-appeal-decision)).

**What this means for 1-10 sessions**
- The selloff is driven by Argentine risk, rates and oil rather than company news, so it can reverse as fast as it came if country risk eases or oil stabilizes.

**VEEV research summary, as of the evening of 2026-11-18**

**Verdict on the story:** The drop looks like sector contagion, not a Veeva-specific event. I found no company news, downgrade or filing that explains it. The stock fell with software on a day the Dow and the S&P 500 were also lower. Earnings on 2026-12-03 are a binary event inside a one-to-ten-session hold.

**Why it fell today (11/18)**
- Software was the weakest group. One recap (Vista Global) put Salesforce down about 9.5%, ServiceNow about 6.5%, Intuit about 7%, and the iShares software ETF (IGV) down more than 3%. These figures came from a single market-wrap source and I couldn't confirm them elsewhere.
- That recap pinned the selling on fears that autonomous AI agents will undercut per-seat software subscriptions. Nothing I found says why that theme hit on this particular day.
- Salesforce is Veeva's main CRM rival, so its plunge hits VEEV as a read-across. The market has treated the pair as linked all year.
- The wider tape was messy. Nvidia reversed its post-earnings gain, the Fed minutes dented the S&P 500, and an Anthropic IPO was reported priced at $83 per share.
- VEEV closed at 277.20, down 3.89%, per Yahoo and CNN. Some other sources quoted different figures, so treat those as noise.
- I found no Veeva press release, downgrade or price-target change dated November 2026. A search for a link to OpenAI's Orchestra Bio acquisition (announced 10/20) found no mention of Veeva. A search tool summary that tied it to today's drop was not supported by the sources.

**Where the stock has been**
- It was about 355 in early 2026. Software then sold off hard on AI-disruption fears, with Anthropic product launches as repeated triggers.
- By late May and June it traded around 170 to 175. Goldman held a Sell rating, cutting its target from 190 to 165 in June, and Citigroup downgraded to Neutral in April.
- Veeva reported fiscal Q2 on 8/26 and the stock jumped about 8 to 9% the next day, to about 266. The recaps put the post-earnings rally at roughly 15%.
- By November it had run to about 290. The 277 close is a pullback within a roughly 60% rebound from the lows. The trend filter in your screen is up, but the whole recovery is only about three months old.

**Fundamentals (fiscal Q2, quarter ended 7/31, reported 8/26)**
- Revenue was $928.0M, up 18%, against a consensus near $904M.
- Subscription revenue was $766.8M, up 16%.
- Non-GAAP operating margin was 44.8%, and non-GAAP EPS was $2.35 against an estimate of $2.22.
- Cash and short-term investments were about $7.2B. Veeva bought back $472.7M of stock in the first half.
- Vault CRM has more than 180 customers live, and 12 of the top 20 biopharmas have committed. Biogen and Regeneron signed in Q2, and Lilly's global rollout was reported in August. Management expects the remaining two top-20 companies to decide by year end.
- Falcon is the new agentic AI platform. Five early adopters are onboarding, with first go-lives planned this year. It is unproven at scale.
- FY27 guidance was raised to revenue of $3.682 to 3.687B and non-GAAP EPS of about $9.21. At 277, that is about 30 times forward earnings by my arithmetic. Net of the $7.2B cash pile, the multiple is a little lower.
- Commercial subscription growth was only about 13%.

**Earnings setup (2026-12-03)**
- Veeva confirmed the date in a 11/12 press release. It reports after the close, with a call at 5:00 PM ET (4:00 PM CT). One calendar site (TipRanks) listed 11/26, which looks stale.
- Q3 guidance (quarter ended 10/31) is revenue of $932 to 935M, non-GAAP operating income of $417 to 420M, and EPS of $2.33 to 2.34.
- At the 11/5 Investor Day, the CFO said Q3 would "meet or exceed" guidance, per an SEC 8-K. A positive pre-announcement lowers the odds of a Q3 miss, but it also means a small beat is already expected.
- Veeva has beaten revenue by about 2.4 to 3.2% over the last four quarters. Consensus EPS ranges from about 2.21 to 2.39 depending on the source.
- The guide for the following quarter and fiscal 2028 comes in the Q4 report, not this one. Q3 commentary on Falcon, the Vault CRM migration pace and Salesforce win-backs is where the stock will move.

- The Yahoo consensus target is about 326, with a Zacks Rank of 3 (Hold). That is a stale-looking, wide-dispersion number. Targets ranged from 165 (Goldman, June) to the 300s earlier in the year. I could not find any target changes from the last two weeks.

- The AI-agent-versus-seat-software theme could keep hitting software through the Dec 3 report, and Veeva is not insulated from it.

- The stock is now below its 50-day average, with RSI at 31. It broke a 20-day low on 2.1 times normal volume, so selling pressure is real.

**HIMS: research summary as of 7:42 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** HIMS is down about 35% in nine sessions. Q3 was a clear miss and the 2026 guidance was cut again. I found no new fundamental news since. The stock looks oversold, but I found no sign yet of a reversal or a bottom. Mixed headlines and thin sourcing mean the bounce case rests mostly on the technicals. The drop in the last few days comes with insider selling and a legal overhang, and peptides are not a near-term revenue source.

**How the drop happened**
- Early November: Lilly deal. Hims can now sell Zepbound ($299/month) and the oral Foundayo ($149/month) on its own platform, matching LillyDirect prices. Hims committed not to compound copies of Lilly drugs. The stock rose more than 7% in premarket on this. Novo's Wegovy and Ozempic have been sold on the platform since March, after Novo's earlier lawsuit over compounded versions.
- Nov 9: The stock closed about $22.98 (down about 11.8% from $26.00) ahead of the report. Sources don't explain that drop. After the report it fell another 16–18% to about $18.8, a seven-month low and the biggest one-day drop since February.
- Nov 17–18: It slid further to about $17.1–17.7. Source prices conflict. Your screen's after-hours print of $17.20 fits that range.

**Q3 results (company 8-K and investor release)**

| Item | Q3 2026 |
|---|---|
| Revenue | $890.4M, up 49%, inside the $880–900M guide; consensus was about $892.8M |
| Gross margin | 57%, versus 74% a year ago and about 64% last quarter |
| Operating loss | $66.1M |
| Net loss | $33M, or about $0.14 a share, against a consensus profit of $0.06 |
| Adjusted EBITDA | $82.4M, against a prior guide of $275–325M for the quarter |
| Subscribers | About 2.8M, down 100k sequentially (up 13% year over year) |
| Free cash flow | $26M |
| Debt versus cash | $1.56B debt versus $712M cash and short-term investments |

- The EBITDA figure of $82.4M for Q3 comes from search summaries, so it is worth confirming against the 8-K.
- Gross margin fell mainly because lower-margin branded weight-loss products are scaling abroad.
- International revenue was $233M, up more than 4x, including about $135M from Eucalyptus.
- One Panabee article showed Q3 revenue of $753M. It contradicts the 8-K, so I ignored it.

**Guidance**
- Full-year 2026 revenue: $3.13–3.15B. Adjusted EBITDA cut to $257–277M, from $275–325M. This is the third profit-target cut this year, per press coverage.
- Q4 revenue: $875–895M. Q4 adjusted EBITDA: $70–90M.
- About $18M of weight-loss membership revenue slipped into Q4.
- Management expects another quarter of subscriber headwinds in Q4.
- It plans to restore US weight-loss marketing before the new year, with Lilly products and multi-month plans. It expects the benefit in Q1.
- Full-year international revenue is expected to be at least $650M, raised from $600M. It targets a $1B run rate in 2027.
- Full-year free cash flow is expected to be positive.
- Longer-term metrics and a 2027 outlook come with the next quarterly report.

**Analysts**
- Needham: Buy, target cut to $32 from $42, blaming lower marketing spend.
- Jefferies: Hold, target cut to $24 from $31. It warned of "heightened stock gyrations."
- Leerink: Market Perform, $25 target. The note is undated.
- KeyBanc: Sector Weight, reiterated Nov 11. It calls 2026 a "transition year" and wants evidence of a growth inflection.
- Canaccord: Buy, $40 target, reiterated Nov 18.
- MarketBeat consensus: Hold, average target about $31.5.
- Ignore the Citi "$11 from $14" item. It is most likely an old note.

**Overhangs**
- The FTC sued on July 29, 2026, with Utah and Los Angeles County as co-plaintiffs. It alleges Hims shared health data with ad platforms and misled users on billing and cancellation. The stock fell 14.7% that day to $25.00.
- A securities class action (Velanki, N.D. Cal.) covers purchases from Aug 4, 2025 to Jul 29, 2026. The lead-plaintiff deadline was Nov 2. Consumer privacy suits are also pending.
- I could not confirm a report that five states joined the FTC suit.
- Insiders sold about $0.44M under 10b5-1 plans on Nov 17 at about $18.53, including the CFO. These are scheduled sales, so the signal is weak, but it is not a vote of confidence at this price.
- Short interest was very high earlier in 2026, about 33.7% in late February. I found no current figure.

**Peptides+ (launched Nov 18)**
- Five compounded treatments: sermorelin, NAD+, glutathione, B12 and L-carnitine. They cost about $150–200 a month including the Care+ membership.
- BPC-157 and TB-500 are planned once regulation allows, with active ingredients made at its California facility.
- Management said peptide revenue will not be material in Q4. Analysts see a slow build over years.
- HHS issued an interim enforcement-discretion policy on Oct 28 covering six peptides. The FDA advisory committee backed those six in July. This is not a final rule, and the FDA still has internal safety concerns.
- The stock was down about 2.9% on launch day, so the launch was not a catalyst.

**Technicals and sentiment (from third-party pages)**
- The stock sits below its 7-, 20- and 50-day averages: about $18.89, $22.82 and $26.54.
- Third-party RSI is about 28 and the lower Bollinger band is about $15.50.
- Support is $17.03, then $16.32. Resistance is $18.57, then $19.40.
- The 52-week range is $13.74–$40.99, and the stock is down about 42–46% year to date.
- Stocktwits retail sentiment moved to "extremely bullish" after the drop. That is a contrarian caution rather than support.
- The Motley Fool piece of Nov 16 is bearish on margins.

- **Upcoming events:** I found no scheduled company event inside the window. FDA or HHS peptide news, Novo or Lilly news, and legal developments are the possible unscheduled catalysts.

agents.report:
SLF is down on a real, specific story: a fund-manager outflow shock plus a disability-claims worry, not a broken business. The two overlap with a pending ex-dividend date inside your window, and I found no news explaining the slide since about Nov 9.

**What happened**
- **Results (Nov 4 after the close, per the company release).** Underlying net income was C$1,146M, up 9%. Underlying EPS was C$2.05, up 10%, and beat consensus of about C$2.01. Underlying ROE was 19.0%.
- **Reported profit fell.** Reported net income was C$785M, down 29%, and reported EPS was C$1.40. Causes were interest-rate impacts of about C$143M, acquisition and restructuring charges of C$126M (GreenOak and Bell Partners), and a C$176M gain a year earlier that did not recur.
- **Dividend and capital.** The dividend was raised to C$1.00 from C$0.96. The capital ratio (LICAT) fell to 142% from 154%, and financial leverage rose to 24.1% from 21.6%. The release does not mention buybacks.
- **The stock fell about 10% on Nov 5.** Tikr, a commentary blog, and Investing.com both report it, along with two downgrades from TD Cowen (to Hold) and National Bank (to Sector Perform). One article put the post-drop TSX price near C$102. A GuruFocus item put the US line at US$73.48. Tikr compared the drop to Sun Life's worst in years, but I could not confirm that.

**Why it fell**
1. **MFS (US asset manager) outflows.** Net outflows were US$26.9B against US$0.9B a year earlier. US$22.6B was retail, and Q2 was already US$22.9B. CEO Kevin Strain said US retail investors "continue to favor passive strategies."
   - MFS is about a quarter of underlying income, and rising markets kept its earnings flat. Tikr argues the 2027 EPS estimate of about C$8.62 is at risk as its asset base shrinks. That is one blog's view, not broker notes.
2. **US group long-term disability.** US experience losses were C$81M, against about C$20M expected by TD Cowen. Consolidated experience losses were C$51M.
   - Strain called it an industry trend. Great-West and Manulife also reported weaker disability results (Manulife Canada core earnings down 4% year to date, Great-West group benefits down 35%). Insurers can reprice, but group premium changes take 12 to 18 months.
3. **Asia.** New-business contractual service margin (CSM, future profit from new sales) fell to C$385M from C$446M, and one source reported the Asia component at C$280M versus C$322M. The company cited a more competitive Hong Kong market. Asia underlying income still rose 7%, and individual insurance sales rose 9%.
4. **Valuation.** Tikr put the stock near 14x forward earnings before the drop, close to a five-year high, and about 12x after it. Its five-year average is 11x. So the multiple had little cushion.

**Positives**
- US underlying income was up 32% (US$141M), led by medical stop-loss and a dental recovery. The August 2025 dental/Medicaid profit warning has largely faded as a worry.
- Scotiabank upgraded to Sector Outperform with a C$122 target. BMO kept a buy-side rating with a target around C$118 (from an earlier CNN/TipRanks listing).
- On Nov 18 the company redeemed C$500M of 2.46% subordinated debentures.
- A Wilton Re reinsurance partnership (announced Aug 25, 2026) is expected to launch in the first half of 2027. It is about US$900M of capital, aiming for US$10B in assets, with Sun Life's asset manager SLC as lead manager. It is not a near-term catalyst.

**What I could not confirm**
- **No news for Nov 10-18.** I found nothing explaining the move from about US$73.8 on Nov 9 to your 71.32 close, which is below the post-earnings level. It looks like drift or sector and market pressure, with a Nov 12-13 TSX dip tied to banks, miners and AI stocks. That is unconfirmed, and the sources mix US and Canadian dollar prices, so check which line each figure refers to.
- **Earnings call.** I found the transcript PDF but could not read its Q&A, so I have no direct management commentary on outflow trends or guidance.
- **Brokers' own notes** were not available, and the National Bank downgrade rationale rests on a secondary summary.

**What to watch over one to ten sessions**
- **Ex-dividend on Nov 25.** The record date is Nov 25 and the payment is Dec 31. C$1.00 is roughly US$0.71, about 1% of the price. Expect that mechanical drop to land inside the window and muddy any bounce.
- **Nov 23 conference.** Jessica Tan has a fireside chat at the Desjardins Toronto Conference, a possible source of management comments on MFS or disability.
- **No earnings catalyst.** Fourth-quarter results are not until about Feb 9, 2027, which Tikr says will show whether outflows slowed.
- **Rebound case.** Earnings beat, dividend raised, no solvency issue, and the price now sits below the 200-day average. A mean-reversion bounce is plausible.
- **Against it.** The thesis damage is structural (MFS outflows are accelerating) and the Nov 5 low has been broken. Nothing is a near-term fix, so there is no turn yet.

agents.report:
**AXON: research summary as of 7:42 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**The story in one line.** AXON missed Q3 on November 5 and cut 2026 guidance because about $130M of federal Dedrone (counter-drone) deployments slipped out of 2026. Management calls this "just a timing piece." The stock fell about 28% from its October 29 close and made new 52-week lows on November 17 and 18. Demand metrics look intact. The weak spots are cash flow, margins and the Skydio funding.

**What happened (Q3 report, Nov 5 after the close)**
- **Revenue and EPS:** Revenue was $908.6M, up 28%, against about $931-937M expected. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.72 against about $1.88-1.90. GAAP EPS was $0.68.
- **Margins:** Gross margin fell to 56.7% from 60.1%. Management cited counter-drone mix, higher memory costs and new product scaling. Adjusted EBITDA was $235.7M, a 25.9% margin.
- **Segments:** Software & Services grew 43% to $437M. Connected Devices grew 16% to $471.5M but fell 7% from the prior quarter. TASER was $233M, down modestly on lower TASER 7 sales.
- **Demand metrics:**
  - Annual recurring revenue was $1.75B, up 40%.
  - Net revenue retention was 126%.
  - Future contracted bookings were $15.8B, up 39%.
  - AI annual recurring revenue passed $100M.
  - Federal bookings are more than five times last year's level year to date.
- **Cash flow:** Free cash flow was -$19M after about $100M of inventory build.
- **Guidance:**
  - 2026 revenue is now $3.61-3.63B (about 30% growth), down from 32-34%.
  - Q4 revenue is guided to $990M-$1.01B, which excludes two large Dedrone deployments of about $100M.
  - Free cash flow is $350-400M, down from $450M.
  - Hitting that range needs roughly $425-475M of free cash flow in Q4 alone, which is more than any full year since at least 2021.
- **Delay cause:** Management blamed slower federal procurement tied to funding and election cycles, plus longer approval and deployment steps. There is no firm ship date. Any deployment completed before December 31 is upside. The transcript does not support a Q1 2027 timing estimate.
- **Reaction:** Per Benzinga and Trefis, the stock fell about 9.8% on the report day and 18.2% on Nov 6, closing at about $313. It slid again on Nov 7.

**Why it may not bounce yet**
- **Skydio cash:** Axon is putting $1.2B into Skydio and now holds about 37% fully diluted. Axon was also named Skydio's exclusive public-safety distributor in the US and Canada. On Nov 16-17 Axon filed to raise the cash share from about 60% to about 90% (about $1.08B), with no Axon shares issued. $127.5M has been paid so far. The call said the deal was partly funded by the $1.15B of 0% convertible notes issued in September (conversion price about $652). The stock fell about 10% on the day those notes launched.
- **Memory costs:** Memory costs are about a 50 basis point margin headwind this year. Management said the 2027 impact will be larger and expects elevated memory prices through 2027 and 2028. One source says the headwind more than quadruples in 2027.
- **Estimates:** Analysts cut 2027 EPS from $10.51 to about $9.44-9.55. Forward P/E is about 36-37x, a five-year low against a five-year average of about 77x. The stock is down about 47% year to date, against SPY up about 8%.
- **Legal:** Several plaintiff firms are soliciting clients for investigations. They ask whether Axon adequately disclosed how much the 2026 outlook rested on a few large federal deployments. These are advertisements, not filed suits, though they could add noise.
- **Insiders:** The only insider activity found was 10b5-1 sales in August ($6.0M and $9.6M, at roughly $574-627). I found no insider buying.
- **Technicals:** The 50-day average is falling toward the 200-day. The stock is about 106% below the average analyst target.

**Analysts**
- **Cuts:** Northland cut its target to $540 from $800 (Outperform). Barclays cut to $507 from $688 (Overweight). Needham cut to $500 from $750 (Buy). JPMorgan cut to $750 (Overweight) in April.
- **Downgrade:** Craig-Hallum downgraded to Hold with a $390 target. This came from a secondary summary, and I did not open the source.
- **Consensus:** About 13 Buy and 4 Hold, average target about $561-612, range about $380-700. Argus, UBS and Northcoast were listed with $600-680 targets.
- **Pattern:** Targets are being cut while ratings are held, which usually means analysts are lagging the price. Stocks that gap down on a guidance cut often keep drifting until the next hard datapoint.

**Price context**
- **Closes:** AXON closed about $306.44 on Nov 16 and $315.42 on Nov 11. It traded as low as $291.11 on Nov 17. Investing.com's 52-week-low piece quotes $291.45, and the figure that matches your screen is $291.11.
- **Last night:** Per your screen, after-hours was 302.10 against a regular close of about 300.6.
- **Moving averages:** MarketBeat on Nov 17 showed the 50-day at $413.60 and the 200-day at $466.47. This is not the same as your screen's 405.68 for the 50-day, because it was taken on a different day.
- **Range:** The 52-week high is $665.07, and the stock is down 52-56% from the August high.
- **Trading data:** Short interest is about 5-6% of shares. Beta is about 1.48.
- **History of similar drops (Trefis, since 2010, small sample):** There have been 8 mature cases of a drop of more than 30% in 30 trading days. The median return after the drop was +8% at 21 trading days and +14% at 63. The median further low after the dip was -13%, and one case fell another 37.6%. This supports a bounce over weeks to months, but not a quick turn.

**Catalysts and calendar**
- **Near term:** Possible Dedrone federal deployments before Dec 31. Skydio cash payments and funding detail. Any plaintiff-firm filing.
- **Q4 report:** Late February, with the 2027 outlook and the Q4 free cash flow of about $450M that the guidance depends on.
- **Product timing:** Body 5 launches next spring. Personal Sensors may pause in Q1 ahead of that. The Apollo Dart TASER product is delayed.
- **Earnings in the 1-10 session window:** None. Next earnings are late February.

**Takeaway for a 1-10 session trade.** The fundamental story is "demand fine, timing and cash slipped," and valuation is the cheapest in five years. Nothing scheduled in the window should force a re-rating. With no earnings in the window, the trade is a pure oversold bounce against a downtrend, with the new low on Nov 17 just 3.7% below the after-hours price. Risks are further drift on the Skydio cash use and the Q4 free cash flow doubt. ATR is 7.0% of price, so moves are wide in both directions.

**Gaps and caveats**
- Benzinga returned 403 errors, so some figures came from search summaries and secondary sites that sometimes conflict.
- I did not find the Nov 18 session driver beyond the Skydio terms change. Verify the Craig-Hallum downgrade, the exact Nov 17-18 closes and the exact 50-day value on your own feed.
- I found nothing on options-market positioning beyond a Benzinga put/call of 1.15.

agents.report:
**HWC: research summary as of 7:42 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**The story in one line:** HWC is a Gulf South regional bank. On Nov 11-12 it announced an all-stock, roughly $3.2B purchase of Trustmark (TRMK), and the market sold it hard. The stock went from about $72.38 to about $65 within days, and our screen has it at 62.05 now. I found no news after Nov 16 that explains the further slide, so the move from about $65 to $62 looks like continued selling on the same story plus sector pressure.

**What happened**
- **Deal terms.** Each Trustmark share converts into 0.7463 HWC shares, about $54.02 per share, an 18.6% premium, and 1.78x tangible book. HWC holders would own about 65% of the combined company.
- **Deal impact.** About 7% dilutive to tangible book value per share, with a 2.8-year earn-back including merger costs. About 7% accretive to 2028 EPS. "Mildly dilutive" to regulatory capital at close.
- **Savings and costs.** $205.5M of annual pretax run-rate cost savings, about 35% of Trustmark's projected 2028 cash expenses. $250M of one-time merger costs. $110M termination fee.
- **Combined bank.** About $58B in assets, about 370 branches, about $40B in loans and $48B in deposits, across six Southeastern states. About 20% market overlap, and about 30 Trustmark branches are within 3 miles of an HWC branch.
- **Timing and approvals.** Close is expected late Q1 2027. It needs regulators and both shareholder bases. Management flagged a possible deposit-concentration issue in one southern Alabama market, about $150M of deposits.
- **Market reaction.** HWC fell about 10.2% on the announcement day. Trustmark rose about 4-5%.
- **Why investors disliked it.** Dilution, a deal "of this size" they didn't expect, integration risk, and a share-funded deal when the buyer's own stock was falling.
- **Piper Sandler (Nov 13).** Cut to Neutral from Overweight, target $88 to $71.50. It models about 2% EPS dilution in 2027 and about 6% accretion in 2028. It said the drop exceeded its expectations and called the franchise attractive over 24 to 36 months.
- **Other analysts.**
  - KBW cut its target from $79 to $72 (market perform).
  - DA Davidson cut from $86 to $80 (Buy).
  - Citi called it a "modest surprise" but favorable, saying synergies are underappreciated.
  - StoneX reiterated Buy at $91.
  - MarketBeat's consensus before the cuts was Moderate Buy, target about $81.
- **Merger-agreement noise.** Amparo Law Firm announced an investigation of whether Trustmark holders got the best price. That is not a lawsuit.

**Background: Q3 (reported Oct 20)**
- **Earnings.** GAAP EPS was $1.36 and adjusted EPS $1.66, in line with the $1.65-$1.66 consensus. One summary says it missed the whisper number.
- **Margin and guidance.** Net interest margin 3.61%, up 5 bp, but about 4 bp of that came from purchase accounting on the One Florida Bank deal. Full-year net interest income guidance was raised to +9-9.5%.
- **Growth.** Organic loan growth slowed to 4% annualized from 10% in Q2. Organic deposits grew 9% annualized.
- **Credit.** Net charge-offs were 16 bp. Criticized commercial loans fell for a seventh straight quarter. Nonaccrual loans rose $19.6M to $133.3M.
- **Capital.** The tangible common equity ratio fell 173 bp to 8.05%, just above management's 8% floor. Tangible book value per share fell from $42.95 to $37.83, driven by the One Florida cash price, unrealized securities losses and buybacks. Buybacks are paused.
- **Prior deal.** One Florida Bank closed Aug 1 (announced May 15). HWC has now done two deals in six months.
- **Dividend.** $0.50 per share quarterly.
- **Insider.** The only insider sale I found was Aug 20, at $76.40. I found no insider buying after the drop.

**Macro and sector**
- Finimize says the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.10% and that regional banks slipped, which hurts share-funded deals. The page is undated, so treat that as unconfirmed.
- Other results mention a Fed hike and higher-for-longer rate fears. They are undated, so I can't pin them to this week.
- I could not find a Nov 18 market wrap, so I don't know how banks traded today.

**Technicals and context**
- The stock is far below its 50-day average (about $72.9 per MarketBeat on Nov 16) and 200-day average (about $71). At 62.05 it is about 15% under the Nov 11 close.
- A figure of about 10x 2027 earnings is Piper's target multiple, not where the stock trades. At $62 the stock is roughly 8.7x Piper's 2027 EPS of $7.15, and well under 1.8x tangible book on the post-Q3 figure of $37.83 (about 1.65x).

**What bears on a 1-10 session trade**
- **For a bounce.** The selling is sentiment about a deal and sector rates, not a credit event. Credit metrics were stable at Q3. Several analysts kept Buy ratings with targets of $72-$91, all well above the price. Oversold readings after a deal-announcement drop often retrace part of the fall.
- **Against.**
  - The deal is a lasting overhang. Nothing resolves it before late Q1 2027, and the next earnings report is Jan 19.
  - The slide continued after Piper's downgrade, so selling hasn't clearly exhausted.
  - Capital is thin (tangible common equity near its floor, buybacks paused), so the company has no buyback to support the stock.
  - Rates look like a headwind if the 10-year really is at 5.10%.
  - Trustmark holders can be expected to hold or sell HWC shares they receive at close, which is a longer-term supply risk.
- **Catalysts inside 10 sessions.** I found none scheduled. An investor presentation, a proxy filing, insider or director buying, or a regulatory comment could appear without notice. The next dividend declaration would normally come in late January.

**Gaps**
- I found no news for Nov 17-18 specific to HWC.
- I could not verify the current 52-week low. The screen says 54.19 and MarketBeat says 55.76.
- I did not find merger-arbitrage spread data or any institutional opposition to the deal.
- Sources disagree on a few details: the deal announcement date (Nov 11 after the close versus Nov 12), GAAP versus adjusted EPS, and one aggregator that put the Q3 stock price near $72. I used the primary SEC filings and the company's headlines where I could.

**FIS (Fidelity National Information Services, still the ticker) as of 7:46 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** FIS is a levered bank-software and processing company that was repriced hard on 2026-11-04 and has kept sliding for two weeks. The damage looks mostly fundamental and is already in the price. I found no catalyst between now and the next 1-10 sessions that would force a turn. A bounce is plausible because the stock is oversold and deeply cheap, but nothing I found would start one. The 11-17 new low and today's weakness suggest sellers are still in control.

**What the company is now**
- On 2026-01-09 FIS closed a swap with Global Payments. It sold its remaining Worldpay stake and bought Global Payments' card-issuer processing business, valued at $13.5B, for the Worldpay stake plus about $7.7B in cash. The new unit is called Total Issuing Solutions.
- Headline revenue growth is mostly this acquisition. Q3 revenue of $3.45B was up 27% reported but only 3.7% pro forma.
- The acquisition added debt. A Substack author who holds the stock calls leverage "the reason the stock is cheap." The stated goal is to trend toward 3.0x gross leverage, and the outgoing CFO would not give a date. The same author says debt is investment grade with about 7x interest coverage. I did not find a total debt figure.

**The 2026-11-04 break (Q3 report)**
- The stock fell 24.06% to $29.61. This was its worst day in years, and the prior biggest drop I found was February 2025.
- Q3 itself was fine. Adjusted EPS was $1.61 against $1.60 expected, and revenue was $3.45B against $3.43B expected.
- The 2026 guide was cut:
  - Adjusted EPS now $5.82-5.89, down from $6.15-6.24.
  - Revenue now $13.445-13.505B, down from $13.63-13.695B.
  - Pro forma growth now 3.1-3.6%, down from 4.5-5%.
- Reasons given:
  - Client-led conversion delays at fewer than 10 large banks. Some restart in Q4 and some slip to Q1 or Q3 of 2027.
  - Bank mergers, with Cadence and Comerica's second account named as lost.
  - Weak Capital Markets license sales as clients move to SaaS.
  - Over $100M of lost non-recurring revenue.
  - Capital markets professional services down 20%.
- The preliminary 2027 framework drags revenue by 250-300 basis points. Sources disagree on the exact headline: one says revenue of -0.5% to +1%, another says 2027 EPS down high single to low double digits. The company says normal growth returns in 2028, and it has called 2027 a "transition year." Management has missed guidance before.
- CFO James Kehoe stepped down. Chief Accounting Officer Alex Brooks is interim CFO from 11-05, and a permanent search is underway. A permanent CFO name is an unscheduled headline risk, and could go either way.
- A portfolio-wide strategic review is under way, with a fuller update promised in early 2027. Capital markets pieces are being shopped for sale, and a prepaid business has already been sold.
- Free cash flow guidance rose while EPS fell. Management expects FCF to keep outpacing net income through 2027, helped by a working-capital program.

**Analysts after the cut**
- Downgrades: BofA to Neutral with a $33 target, RBC to Sector Perform, Argus to Hold, and Zacks to Strong Sell.

- Market cap is about $14.3B.
- About 5x 2026 adjusted EPS and 5.6x the 2027 trough.
- About 6.3x EV/EBITDA.
- FCF yield about 14%, by the Substack author's math.
- Dividend is $0.44 per quarter, about a 6.3% yield. Ex-date and record date are 12/14 and payment is 12/28. The dividend takes about 41% of FCF.

**DDOG research as of 7:42 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** DDOG has fallen about 45% from its ~$300 high on two guidance disappointments, both tied to one AI customer, plus a software-sector selloff. Growth, cash flow and EPS are all strong. The market is pricing the risk that more AI customers cut back. No new catalyst is scheduled before the Q4 report in February. For a 1-10 session trade, that makes this a sentiment and sector-beta bounce candidate, not a fundamental turn.

**Story so far**
- **Aug 6 (Q2 report):** Revenue grew 36% to $1.12B. Datadog said its largest AI customer would cut usage in the second half. That customer had just signed a nine-figure renewal, and analysts widely assume it is OpenAI. Datadog has not confirmed the name. The stock fell 14-19%. AI-native accounts were about 11% of Q2 revenue.
- **Oct 29-30:** ServiceNow fell about 27% on slower contracted growth and AI-disruption fears. DDOG fell about 11% on Oct 30 on sector selling, with no company news. It closed at about $236 that day, down from $265.84. The same article put its 200-day average near $197.60.
- **Nov 4 (Q3 report):**
  - **Q3 results:** Revenue was $1.197B, up 35% and $52M above the top of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.81 versus $0.64 expected. Free cash flow was $251M (21% margin). About 4,860 customers spend over $100K, up 20%, and there are over 850 AI customers.
  - **Guidance:** Full-year revenue was raised to $4.515-4.525B. Q4 revenue is guided to $1.19-1.20B, which is flat to slightly down from Q3 and about 25-26% year-over-year growth. Q4 EPS guidance of $0.69-0.71 is above the $0.64 consensus.
  - **Why it hurt:**
    - The largest customer cut usage in Q3 but stayed above its minimum commitment. The Q4 guide assumes it spends only the minimum.
    - Several large AI customers renewed early at higher commitments but lower per-unit pricing. Management called this a short-term headwind. It gave no dollar figure.
    - Management said that excluding the largest customer, implied Q4 growth is in the low-to-mid 30s. Growth from non-AI customers is in the high 20s, accelerating for a fifth straight quarter.
    - Truist said the guide "continues to disappoint."
  - **Move:** The stock fell about 14%, from roughly $220 before the report.
- **Nov 5:** It fell another 7.5% to a $174.60 close as AI stocks slid. Cloudflare then reported strong results and rose 9.9% on Nov 6.
- **Nov 9 close:** $179.62.
- **Nov 16:** One source has about $174.56, down about 5%. The November low cited is $170.50.
- **Nov 17:** IGV (the software ETF) fell more than 3% and Salesforce nearly 10%, on fears that AI agents will cut software seat counts. One source says DDOG fell 5.3% to $163.72. That conflicts with your screen's close of about $167 (implied by 171.71 being up 2.8%). Treat the exact levels as unreliable.
- **Tonight:** Nvidia beat estimates and rose about 2% after hours. That fits the bounce in DDOG after hours. I found no DDOG-specific news for Nov 18.

**Analysts**
- Most cut targets but kept ratings after Q3. I found no major downgrade tied to the report.
  - Bernstein: $273 from $350, Outperform.
  - Morgan Stanley: $270, Overweight.
  - Barclays: $262.
  - Cantor: $260.
  - Scotiabank: $260.
  - Stifel: $245.
  - Citi: $290, Buy.
  - CIBC: $285.
  - Jefferies: $230, citing customer concentration.
  - Truist: $300, Buy.
- Citi said the selloff is "likely missing forest-for-the-trees."
- Goldman is a Sell with a $171 target. Its bear case is that if one big AI customer can cut back, another can too.
- The consensus target is about $272-278, far above the current price.
- Weiss rates it Sell (D).

**Valuation**
- Forward P/E was about 60-66x after the Nov 5 drop and 81x on Nov 2. The five-year average is about 102-104x. The price has fallen further since, so the multiple is lower now.
- The 2027 EPS estimate rose to $3.16 from $2.98.

**Risks**
- **Customer risk:** Guggenheim argued in 2025 that OpenAI could build its own tooling. Hunterbrook reported in 2026 that an unnamed foundation-model company, which analysts guess is Anthropic, consolidated onto Datadog. That cuts the other way.
- **Sector risk:** Software is under pressure from AI-disruption worries, with the Anthropic IPO cited as a factor. Further software selling could push DDOG lower.
- **Insider selling:** Insiders sold about $208M of stock over the 90 days to late October. Some of it was under pre-set 10b5-1 plans.

- **Business:** OpenText is shrinking overall but growing in cloud. Q1 FY27 (reported Nov 5) revenue was $1.237B, down 4.0%. Core revenue was $864M, up 2.4%, and core cloud was $339M, up 11.2%. Content Cloud grew 20.7%.

  - Large cloud deals (over $1M) rose only 6% to 35.

- **Reclassification:** About $116M of quarterly revenue was moved from core to non-core, which flatters core growth. Management said more reclassifications could follow.

**ARWR research summary, as of the 2026-11-18 close.** I found no news dated Nov 18 or Nov 17 beyond the analyst note below. Nothing I found explains the slide to 43.11 after the Nov 13 close at 47.78 (a catalyst could still exist that I missed), and no source gave short interest after October. The Nov 17 close of 42.88 comes from a MarketBeat auto-alert.

**The story: a sell-off on rival Ionis's sHTG launch, not an Arrowhead failure**
- Arrowhead's plozasiran (REDEMPLO) is approved for familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS, a rare triglyceride disease). The real prize is severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG, a much larger market).
- On Nov 9, Ionis reported Q3 sales of $9M for Tryngolza, its rival drug in sHTG, and cut 2026 sales guidance to about $50M from $100–110M. Ionis fell about 21%.
- ARWR closed at $58.16 on Nov 6 and gapped to $52.49 on Nov 9. It traded around $48.65 mid-session, with one source citing a $49.24 close.
- It then slid further on fiscal Q4 results on Nov 12, closed Nov 13 at $47.78 (down 17.8% on the week), and sat at $42.88 on Nov 17. The 52-week range is $37.06–$95.49, with a high of $90.97 in mid-August.
- Stifel cut its target to $96. Citi cut to $105 and RBC held $100, both keeping bullish ratings. Consensus target is about $99 (Moderate Buy), and Weiss rates it sell.
- Jefferies called the setup "tricky", saying Arrowhead must disprove negative sentiment, and noted its earlier-stage programs lack a single near-term catalyst.

**Fiscal Q4 (Nov 12)**
- The quarter was a big miss. EPS was -$3.04 versus about -$1.59 expected, and revenue was $37.8M versus about $66M expected.
- The full-year net loss was $724M ($5.11 per share), including a $215M expense for a purchased priority review voucher (a transferable ticket for faster FDA review). Revenue was $450.8M, down from $829.4M because of one-time Sarepta collaboration revenue in the prior year.
- REDEMPLO's first-year product revenue was only about $6.6M (from secondary sources). The press release gives no dollar figure.
- The launch funnel is growing:
  - Weekly prescriptions are about 50–60, up from 20–30 a quarter earlier.
  - Cumulative new-to-brand prescriptions were 950 at quarter-end and passed 1,250 by early November.
  - There are 860+ prescribers and about 160M covered lives.
- Management calls the conversion from prescription to paid shipment a "choke point". There is no revenue guidance.

**Balance sheet**
- Total cash resources are about $1.19B, down about $400M in the quarter. Operating cash burn was $272M for the year, and stockholders' equity is only $50M.
- There is $683M of convertible notes (0%, due 2032) and a new $400M Sixth Street term loan. The loan is at SOFR+5.5% instead of 15%, matures in 2031, and has no cash sweeps. Nothing is due before late 2031.
- No cash runway figure was given. Selling the priority review voucher could add roughly $180–220M. No sale agreement exists.
- The company raised about $800M in January 2026, selling common stock at $64.50. This is below that level now, so a further raise at these prices would be dilutive. The $64.50 level could act as overhead resistance.

**Catalysts in or near your 1–10 session window**
- **FDA action date for sHTG:** The sHTG supplemental application was filed Nov 2. It was accepted into the FDA's STAR pilot, which allows a six-month priority review. Management said the FDA action date should be set within about 50 days of filing, which the call-summary writer inferred means late December. This is not confirmed.
- **Launch timing:** The target is a Q2 2027 launch, versus a second-half 2027 approval expected before the pilot acceptance. The $45,000-per-year price is the same for FCS and sHTG.
- **Obesity programs:** ARO-ALK7 data are due by year-end 2026. Earlier ARO-INHBE obesity data were positive in January, but mixed reports on the stock's reaction conflict.
- **Other timing:** Beyond that, the next events are the ARO-MAPT trial applications around end-2026 or early 2027 and the zodasiran Phase 3 readout in the second half of 2027.
- **Reporting dates:** A Form 10-QT covering Oct 1 – Dec 31 will follow the fiscal year change to Dec 31, effective Jan 1, 2027. The next quarterly report is therefore unlikely before February 2027.

**Risks and doubts**
- Ionis's weak launch is the live question. Management blames Ionis's communication and execution, and says it doesn't change their sHTG expectations. That is management's view, and the market doesn't agree.
- In the sHTG trials, worsening glycemic control occurred in 14.3% of treated patients versus 8.7% on placebo.
- Broad sHTG uptake depends on payer policies and will take years.
- Short interest was about 10.8M shares (5.7 days to cover) in late October, before the drop. I found nothing more recent.

**Read for the trade:** The selloff is a sentiment and sector reset, and the fundamentals did not break. Financing risk is low and the pipeline is intact. The 43.11 close is just above the 20-day low of 42.07 and the 52-week low of 37.06. Nothing found suggests a turn has started. The upside catalyst is the FDA action date, which may land in late December and so could fall outside a 1–10 session hold. Further weakness could come from continued Ionis-related headlines, analyst target cuts, or tax-loss selling in biotech.

**UUP and the dollar: the story as of 7:46 PM CT, Wednesday 2026-11-18**

The dollar rally is a repricing of Fed hikes, not a safe-haven spike. The December hike is about 90% priced and the market is still extending, so nothing visible argues for fading this over one to ten sessions. The risks to the long side are binary events and a Japanese yen intervention.

**What drives the dollar**
- **Fed hikes:** The Fed cut three times in late 2025. It then hiked 25 bp on Sept 16 to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike since 2023. It held in October on a 10–2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Chair Warsh has been hawkish since Jackson Hole in August.
- **Inflation:** October CPI rose 0.4% (September 0.6%), beating forecasts for a third straight month. Core CPI was 0.3%. October PPI was 6.5% year on year against 6.6% expected. The dollar barely moved on PPI (sources conflict on core PPI). Payrolls were +165K with unemployment at 4.1%.
- **Pricing:** CME FedWatch puts the December 9 decision at about 90% for 25 bp and about 10% for 50 bp. Futures see the policy rate midpoint near 4.15% after the meeting and about 4.73% by September 2027. Goldman expects hikes in December and March. Deutsche Bank expects December, January and March.
- **Yields:** The 2-year was about 4.80–4.84% and the 10-year about 5.07%. A 20-year auction today priced at 5.459%, a high for the year.
- **Today's catalyst:** The October FOMC minutes said almost all participants expect more hikes. A couple were open to a move above 25 bp in December. Waller called for 50 bp or a stronger tightening signal. Williams and Musalem also leaned hawkish.
- **Dollar level:** DXY made a new high near 103.9 today, its highest since April 2025. It was about 102.9 on Nov 11 and about 103.1–103.2 on Nov 12–13. It is up about 8% from the January low.
- **Other currencies:** The euro is at about 1.097, its lowest since spring 2025. That is despite two ECB hikes (deposit rate 2.50%, eurozone inflation 4.0%). The pound fell and the Australian dollar is at lows since January. USD/JPY is about 159.4, pinned just under 160.

**What looks stretched**
- **Rally basis:** Analysts say it rests "almost exclusively" on Fed expectations, and the hikes are expected, not yet delivered. Much of it is priced.
- **Yen intervention:** The USD/JPY 160 line has been tested three times this year. Japan spent about ¥27.1 trillion across the spring and summer rounds, with a record ¥6.28 trillion in one day on April 30. The US Treasury joined on July 31, its first yen buy since 1998. The yen is the second-largest DXY component, so a repeat could knock the index down quickly.
- **BoJ:** A hike to 1.5% is expected on Dec 17–18.
- **Gold:** Gold fell about 3% to about $3,727 today, a 14-month low, and silver fell about 4.8%. The two are moving inversely to the dollar.
- **Risk assets:** The S&P 500 has fallen five sessions in a row. Bitcoin fell 3.7% to about $62.5K. Oil fell 3.2% to $83.26 on an inventory build, but Hormuz and Iran risks persist. Some analysts credit the war with part of the safe-haven bid.
- **Forecasts:** The 2025 consensus had the dollar falling through 2026, and the rally has already recovered most of the 2025 tariff-shock losses. These are stale views, but the rally has gone against them.

**UUP itself**
- It holds US Dollar Index futures, with an expense ratio of 0.75–0.78% (sources differ).
- It closed at $29.50 on Nov 13, with a 52-week range of $26.39–$29.50. Our screen has a prior high of 29.57, a close near 29.61, and an after-hours print of 29.73. UUP is liquid, but a small fund, with reported AUM from about $103M to $480M depending on the source.
- UUP is just a DXY proxy, so fade or hold decisions depend on the dollar's path. Any yen or euro reversal hits it directly.

**Upcoming events**
- **Soon:** Jobless claims Thursday; Lagarde speaks Thursday; Fed speakers all week.
- **Dates:** The Fed decides Dec 9 (the meeting is Dec 8–9), the ECB and BoJ meet in December (BoJ Dec 17–18), and Lagarde leaves Feb 7.
- **Mid-December risk:** A half-point December hike would widen the rate gap and likely extend the dollar. It would also raise the chance of Japanese intervention.

agents.report:
**Card lenders (AXP, COF, SYF): research as of 7:42 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line.** The 20-session underperformance against XLF has an identifiable cause. It is policy risk from the post-midterm shift: Democrats won Congress and Warren is pushing a 10% rate cap with Trump's possible help. A fundamentals problem does not explain the drop. Q3 results were mostly good. Reported credit trends are stable to improving, though the Fed is expected to hike on Dec 9. The policy overhang has no near-term resolution date, so it argues against a confident mean-reversion long over 1-10 sessions.

**What happened**
- **Policy shock, Nov 3 to 17.**
  - Democrats won the Senate in the midterms and will control both chambers in January 2027.
  - On Nov 8, Warren said on Face the Nation she is "ready to go" on a 10% card APR cap and wants to work with Trump. She is expected to chair Senate Banking.
  - Trump's January call for a one-year 10% cap had no legal force. The Jan 20 date passed with nothing enacted.
  - Some Republicans, including Thune, have been reluctant, and Trump has threatened to be "Mr. Veto". A Nov 17 R Street piece says Democrats expect Trump to cooperate.
  - As of Nov 19, I found no law or executive order, and no voluntary bank commitment.
- **Market reaction to the cap talk was small.** The Monday after Warren's interview, COF fell 1.1%, BFH 2.9%, SYF 0.1% and AXP rose 1.1%. The January precedent was much larger: COF fell about 6%, SYF and BFH 8-10%, AXP about 4-5%. The market looks like it is discounting this with a lag, not panicking.
- **Dispersion by company.**
  - Bloomberg Intelligence and Wells Fargo said a cap would hit COF, SYF and Bread hardest, and AXP less because its customers are affluent. Wells Fargo said a one-year 10% cap could "wipe out earnings" for card-focused lenders.
  - A Nov 11 bank note estimated a 36% cap would cut EPS only 2-3%. A 10-18% cap would be far worse.
  - This is why AXP is not trading like COF or SYF. The equal-weight basket mixes two different risk profiles.
- **Other drags**
  - AXP fell 3.5% intraday on Nov 5 with no stated cause.
  - AXP slipped after its Oct 23 Q3 report despite a beat and a guidance raise (reported EPS guide $18.30-18.60). Revenue and network volume slightly missed, commercial spending growth was only 3%, and there was a $336M restructuring charge. It is around $315, near the low end of its 52-week range ($291-$387).
  - COF fell 3.15% on Nov 17. The only source is an auto-generated TradingKey piece citing consumer-credit worries, margins, Discover integration costs and insider sales. I could not confirm a specific trigger.
  - Older AI and agentic-commerce fears hit AXP, COF and SYF in February.
- **Macro backdrop.**
  - The Fed is about to hike. October FOMC minutes (released Nov 18) showed almost all participants saw further hikes as appropriate. Roughly 91-100% odds are priced for a 25 bp hike on Dec 9, and Waller floated 50 bp.
  - The 10-year yield is about 5.07%.
  - XLF fell 1.14% today to about 56.43, with banks weak. Today's +0.5% basket gain against XLF is mostly the sector falling, not the card names rising.

**Fundamentals (Q3, reported in October)**
- **Synchrony.**
  - EPS was $2.68 against $2.42 expected.
  - The net charge-off rate fell to 4.79%.
  - Purchase volume was up 8%.
  - FY26 EPS guide is about $9.50, the top of its range, but implied Q4 is slightly below the Street. Management said Q3 is not a new run rate.
  - Evercore downgraded it to In-Line (target $78), and UBS stayed Neutral (target $80).
  - The Walmart/OnePay portfolio losses ramp through 2027.
  - Deposit betas are expected to be higher in this hiking cycle.
  - The stock was about $71-74 in early to mid-November, below its 200-day average. I could not confirm today's close.
- **Capital One.**
  - Adjusted EPS was $6.69 against about $5.50 expected.
  - The domestic card charge-off rate fell to 3.98%, and there was a $225M reserve release.
  - Discover integration is ahead of schedule. Cumulative cost is $2.4B, with $338M in Q3.
  - The stock is around $186. Consensus target is about $252-256.
  - There was insider selling, including by Fairbank.
- **American Express.** It has the lowest charge-offs in its peer group and a forward P/E of about 16. Berkshire owns 22.6%.
- **Credit data.**
  - The NY Fed Q3 report (Nov 10) showed card balances at a record $1.29T.
  - The share of card balances newly entering serious delinquency fell for a third quarter, to 6.9%. Overall household delinquency rose to 5.0%, led by mortgages.
  - October bank-level card delinquencies ticked up to 2.68% from 2.62%.
  - Stress is concentrated in low-income areas, which matters most for SYF and COF.

**Other policy item.** The Credit Card Competition Act (S.3623) has no floor vote. It faces an uncertain future after Marshall's defeat and Durbin's retirement. There is renewed talk of capping interchange in 2027. That is a bigger issue for the networks than for these lenders.

**Implications for a 1-10 session long of the basket against XLF**
- **For:**
  - Earnings and credit were solid.
  - The group is near 52-week lows and looks oversold.
  - Cap legislation is unlikely before January 2027 and still has to get past a presidential veto.
  - Banks (XLF) are also under rate pressure.
  - Walmart earns on Nov 19 (before the open), which is relevant to SYF's Walmart portfolio and consumer health.
- **Against:**
  - There is no catalyst that removes the cap overhang within 10 sessions. More headlines from Warren, Trump or Truth Social are likely, and each is a downside shock for COF and SYF.
  - Volatility is elevated at 1.75 times normal.
  - A Dec 9 hike and higher deposit costs hurt lenders. The relative stretch against XLF could widen if XLF stabilizes.
  - AXP and COF/SYF have different sensitivity to a cap, so the basket hedge is imperfect.
- **Caution.** I could not find a precise cause for the Nov 17 COF drop. I also could not confirm SYF's Nov 18 close or SYF's recent price path.

**VIST research brief, as of 7:46 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** The weakness looks like macro and oil risk repricing, not a company problem. Operations and the balance sheet are strong. Sellers have been driven by Argentina country risk, falling oil, and Goldman's higher discount rate. Nothing I found marks a turn yet, and several of the same pressures are still live. Several sources conflict on numbers, which I flag below.

**What happened to the price**
- **Level:** The NYSE close was about $51.9. MarketBeat showed $52.73 intraday, down $1.23 on 216k shares against a 1.24M average. Google Finance showed $51.93, -3.75%. Infobae and other outlets put the day's drop at about 3.8%.
- **Path since earnings:** The stock closed at $72.27 on Oct 28, so it is down about 28% in three weeks.
- **Averages:** MarketBeat lists the 50-day at $67.55 and the 200-day at $67.20, so the 50-day is only just under the 200-day. The stock crossed below its 200-day around Nov 3.
- **Valuation:** P/E is about 7.3, beta is 0.58, and the market cap is $5.8B.
- **Earlier drops:** It fell 3.7% to $55.60 on Nov 10, and Zacks called it oversold on Nov 12 after a 16.8% decline over four weeks.

**Why it is falling (no single company event found)**
1. **Argentina risk repricing.**
   - Riesgo país was 808 on Nov 2, about 880 on Nov 9 (a one-year high), and 848 on Nov 18. That is up about 8% in November.
   - Argentine ADRs fell hard on Nov 18 (Infobae called it external contagion). Cresud fell 6.7%, Galicia hit its lowest level since September 2025, and YPF fell 3.6%.
   - One analyst estimates the Merval in dollars is down about 34% from its July high.
   - The CCL-to-official dollar gap is the widest since October 2025. Over $20B of debt matures through 2027, with presidential elections in between.
2. **Goldman cut targets on Nov 17.**
   - Vista went to $69.70 from $81.50, and YPF to $48.70 (Hold).
   - The reason was a higher discount rate on Argentine assets. The 2028 EV/EBITDA multiple fell from 3.8x to 3.4x.
   - Goldman's Brent deck is $91.82 for 2026, $75 for 2027 and $70 for 2028.
   - Even so, it prefers Vista to YPF because Vista is less exposed to local macro, and it estimates a 15% 2028 free cash flow yield at $75 Brent.
3. **Oil is sliding from its peaks.**
   - Brent settled at $95.84 on Nov 13, its second straight weekly loss. It was about $91.8-92.9 on Nov 18.
   - Reuters-based reports said Brent fell 16% in the week before Nov 13 as the Iran war risk eased, and the IEA now sees a Q4 surplus of about 1.7M bpd.
   - US crude stocks rose 5.3M barrels. Hormuz and Iran incidents were still being reported on Nov 18, so the geopolitical premium is two-sided.
4. **Q3 earnings were a small disappointment.** EPS of $2.16 missed the $2.79 consensus, revenue beat, and the shares slipped about 2.5%. Part of the EPS gap is a $211.8M tax charge, and the prior-year net income included a one-off $288M gain.

**Fundamentals (Q3, reported Oct 28)**
- **Production:** 169,023 boe/d, up 33% year over year (about 13 points organic, about 20 from the Equinor assets). Oil was 147k bbl/d. One CEO quote in the transcript says 159k; I treat that as an error.
- **Realized oil price:** $84.20/bbl, down 6% from the prior quarter. Brent averaged $91.3 in Q3.
- **Earnings:** Revenue was $1.234B and adjusted EBITDA was $841.5M (68% margin).
- **Cash and capex:** Free cash flow was $334M on $460M of capex. Lifting cost was $4.7/boe.
- **Debt:** Net debt was $2.86B and net leverage 1.12x, with a year-end target of about 1.0x.
- **Buyback:** $55M was spent in Q3, leaving $95M of a $150M 2026 plan. There is no dividend.
- **Q4:** Production is expected flat in October and November, with the "170k" soft guidance possibly reaching about 175k.
- **2027 guidance, reiterated:** 185k boe/d and $3.3B EBITDA at $80 Brent. Each $1 of Brent moves EBITDA by about $45-50M. A fuller 2027 capex update comes with Q4 results in February.
- **VMOS pipeline:** Mechanical completion is due at year-end, with fill in Q1 and commercial operation in the first half of 2027. Initial capacity is 80k bbl/d. Vista has 180k bbl/d of current capacity, with 36k spare.
- **RIGI:** If its application is approved, Bandurria Norte moves from 2029 to 2027 and activity could reach the high end of the 100-110 well plan.

**Company-specific risks**
- **Unpaid tax:** Finsee flags income tax payable of $411M (against $121M in December), with only $50M paid in Q3 versus a $247M charge. The call transcript did not discuss it.
- **Hedges:** Oil hedges have lost $134M over nine months.
- **Concentration:** YPF-run blocks are 45% of production.
- **Costs:** Peso inflation is raising unit costs.
- **Earn-out:** The Equinor earn-out liability is about $308M.

**Analysts**
- **UBS (Nov 18):** Target raised to $100 from $80, Buy.
- **JPMorgan:** Cut to $87 on Oct 29, Overweight.
- **Others:** Zacks upgraded to Strong Buy on Oct 30. Weiss and Wall Street Zen cut their ratings on Nov 9 and Nov 15.
- **Consensus:** About $82-85, mostly Buy.
- **Goldman:** $69.70, the lowest of the large houses, and it still sits above the price.
- **Source conflict:** A pricetargets.com snapshot showed a $68 average with Goldman at $53.20. It is undated and probably stale.

**Setup for the next 1-10 sessions**
- **Rebound case:**
  - The screen shows RSI 24 and a -4 ATR stretch.
  - Brent is still above the $80 that 2027 guidance assumes.
  - The valuation is cheap and the buyback is live.
  - Analyst targets sit well above the price.
  - A bounce in Argentine bonds and ADRs, or oil stabilizing, would help.
- **Against:**
  - There is no reversal signal yet. The stock is making new lows, with the 20-day low at $53.19 and the 52-week low at $43.71 about 16% below.
  - Contagion from Argentine ADRs and the dollar gap is ongoing.
  - Oil has a supply-surplus narrative behind it.
  - Goldman's 2027 deck of $75 is below the $80 in guidance.
  - Estimate-revision pressure from the discount-rate change has probably not run its course.
- **Catalysts to watch:**
  - Brent and Iran/Hormuz headlines.
  - Riesgo país around 850.
  - Argentine October trade data from INDEC on Nov 19.
  - Argentine financing news on the repo, the return to international markets, and the PASO primaries.

**What happened**
- **The drop:** CRM fell about 9.4% on Tue Nov 17, from $214.83 to about $194.5–194.6. That was its worst day since May 2024 and its lowest close since mid-August. There was no company news ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262310309-salesforce-worst-day-since-2024-ai-fears-software-selloff-189-50-support-november-18-2026-tradingkey), [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/crm/articles/626280/what-moved-salesforce-stock/2026-11-18)).

- **Peers:** The selloff was sector-wide. ServiceNow fell about 6.5–7%, HubSpot about 6.8%, Intuit about 6.4%, and Workday about 5%. The iShares software ETF fell 4.4%. Fifty-seven of 62 application-software peers fell. The Dow lost about 860 points, and the S&P and Nasdaq had their first four-day losing streak since September ([MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/salesforce-and-servicenow-fall-as-software-stocks-slide-again-a-day-before-anthropic-prices-its-ipo/)).
- **Relative weakness:** CRM fell more than 3x the median software peer, and more than any of its five closest peers (Trefis).

**Why, as reported**
1. **AI agents cutting per-seat licenses.** An RBC analyst said on a podcast that AI companies could seriously harm Salesforce.
2. **Anthropic IPO timing.** It prices Nov 18, with trading expected Nov 19 as ANT. The roadshow range was $70–78 a share, raising up to about $64B. Commentators suggest investors are selling seat-priced software to fund it (MLQ, [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/articles/624620/is-the-anthropic-ipo-bad-news-for-salesforce-and-servicenow-stock/2026-11-12)).
   - I could not confirm that it priced or debuted.
   - One report says Salesforce's Anthropic stake is about 45% of its $11.3B strategic investment portfolio (MLQ).
3. **Fund positioning.** A Bank of America survey showed fund managers cutting tech at the fastest pace since 2006 (MLQ).
4. **Doubts about Agentforce and deal spending.** These include how fast Agentforce adds revenue, and the Braze purchase.
5. **Sector contagion.** ServiceNow has been sliding since its Oct 28 report, when its cRPO guidance missed. It is about 46% below its 52-week high (MLQ).

**Fundamentals (fiscal Q2, reported Aug 26)**
- **Results:** Revenue was $11.3B, up 11%, including $456M from Informatica (the data-management company Salesforce bought). Organic growth is estimated at only about 7–8%. cRPO (contracted revenue not yet recognized) was $33.5B, up 14%. Non-GAAP EPS was $5.90.
