# STLA research (as of the evening of 2026-11-18)

**Bottom line:** The slide has a clear cause and no near-term catalyst to reverse it. The shares are down about 65% year to date. The story is a failed EV strategy, cash burn, and now rising cost warnings for 2027–28. The $3.55 after-hours price is a new record low, a break below the 20-day low of 3.61, with a fresh downgrade and a Canadian legal dispute adding pressure. A mean-reversion bounce is plausible over 1–10 sessions, but nothing I found would trigger one. The next real catalysts are the Canada deadline in mid-December, year-end sales and February results.

## Price and tape
- STLA closed at $3.71 on Nov 16, down 2.9% on the day. That is 65.9% below the $10.89 year-end 2025 level ([ClubAlfa](https://www.clubalfa.it/en/stellantis-stock-falls-65-9-in-2026-as-new-downgrade-adds-pressure-47934)).
- On Nov 18 it hit a new 52-week low of $3.52. It last traded at $3.543 against a prior close of $3.64, on 4.7M shares. The 50-day average is $4.51 and the 200-day is $6.27 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-stellantis-nyse-stla-sets-new-52-week-low-after-analyst-downgrade-2026-11-18/)).
- The slide has been steady:
  - $3.95 on Oct 23, after a 7.5% one-day drop to a record low ([24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/23/stellantis-at-record-low-turnaround-play-or-value-trap/)).
  - A bounce to about $4.54 in early November, and about $4.11 on Nov 11.
  - Then lower lows through the week.
- In Paris the stock hit €3.40 on Nov 16, a five-year low. It was 12% below its 20-day average and 15.8% below its 50-day, and had lost about 62% over one year ([Idéal Investisseur](https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/stellantis-shares-hit-a-five-year-low-and-close-last-in-the-cac-40/29421.html)).
- The Paris close was €3.31 on Nov 17 (down 1.8%), and the Lang & Schwarz quote was €3.27 on the morning of Nov 18 ([ad-hoc-news](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/stellantis-faces-twin-downgrades-as-cost-pressures-mount-and-canada-demands-answers/70531568)). Market cap is under €10B.
- Valuation is cheap on paper: about 6.4x current-year and 3.6x next-year earnings (consensus figures in the Idéal Investisseur piece). That is the "value trap or turnaround" debate.

## How it got here
1. **EV reset.** On Feb 26 Stellantis reported a €22.3B loss for 2025, driven by €25.4B in charges to reset its EV plans. The CEO called it "the cost of over-estimating the pace of the energy transition." The 2026 dividend was suspended ([24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/03/stellantis-is-now-down-58-in-2026-is-stla-stock-dead-money-or-the-opportunity-of-a-lifetime/)).
2. **Hybrid bonds.** In March it issued a large hybrid-bond package to shore up the balance sheet. The figure is reported as both €5B and €3.665B. Exor did not take part, and I found no rights-issue reports ([Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/stellantis-market-the-hybrid-bond-first-tranche-22-billion-AIkabMtB)).
3. **Capital Markets Day, May 21.** The "FaSTLAne 2030" plan:
   - about €60B of investment and 60+ new products;
   - €6B in annual savings by 2028;
   - focus on Jeep, Ram, Peugeot and Fiat;
   - heavy reliance on partners (Leapmotor, Dongfeng, Tata/JLR).

   The shares fell on the day, and Intermonte said the recovery path was delayed by about a year ([BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/2026/05/21/stellantis-unveils-us70-billion-strategy-pivot-under-filosa-markets-wary/)).
4. **Summer downgrades.**
   - UBS cut to neutral on Aug 3 and cut its target by almost 40%.
   - Bernstein cut to underperform on Aug 7.
   - Morgan Stanley cut to underweight on Sept 14.
   - Piper Sandler is at underweight with a $4 target.
   - Q2 North American margin was weak, and first-half adjusted operating income fell 94%.
5. **Q3 results, Oct 28** ([Futurum](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/stellantis-q3-fy-2026-earnings-show-cost-cuts-offsetting-a-weak-europe/)):
   - Revenue was €37.6B (up 1%). Adjusted operating income was €256M, a 0.7% margin. The net loss was €453M.
   - North America returned to a €64M profit on pricing (Ram 1500 US sales up 73%) despite a 12% drop in shipments from planned Jeep downtime.
   - Europe swung to a €311M loss on negative pricing and a heavy battery-EV mix.
   - Industrial cash outflow was €4.0B in the quarter. Industrial liquidity is €42.7B.
   - Guidance was reaffirmed: low-single-digit margin in 2026 and positive industrial free cash flow in 2027. Full-year tariff cost is about €1B.
   - The savings program has delivered €828M, with Q4 expected in the mid-hundreds of millions of euros. Management warned these are gross of commodity and chip inflation.
   - Q4 guidance included extra costs for memory chips and recalls.
   - The stock bounced on the print, then gave it all back.
6. **The cost warning, Nov 12.** At an Italian parts-industry event, CEO Filosa warned of "significant raw material inflation" in 2027 and probably 2028, plus higher memory-chip, circuit-board and semiconductor costs, "measured in billions of euros." A spokesperson said this referred to the company's whole annual cost base ([TimesLIVE/Reuters](https://www.timeslive.co.za/motoring/2026-11-13-stellantis-warns-of-billions-in-rising-supplier-costs/)).
7. **Downgrades, Nov 17–18.** Oddo BHF cut to underperform with a €3 target, the lowest on the street, down from €4.50. It sees an extra gross cost burden of about €2.2B in 2027 and says consensus margin recovery is too optimistic. LBBW cut from buy to hold with a €3.50 target. Bloomberg's tally was 4 buy, 20 hold and 7 sell, with an average target of €4.94 ([Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/stellantis-stock-hits-fresh-alltime-lows-after-oddo-bhf-downgrade-93CH-5709081)). MarketBeat's US consensus is "Reduce" with an average target of $6.97, so most targets sit far above the price.

## Live issues
- **Canada and Brampton.** Stellantis agreed on Nov 9 to sell the idled Brampton plant to the armoured-vehicle maker Roshel, closing by year-end subject to conditions. Ottawa issued a formal default notice on Nov 12 under a 2022 funding agreement. It gave 30 days to cure (about Dec 12) and says Stellantis could owe hundreds of millions. Stellantis offered to repay C$24M. Governments and Unifor are seeking a meeting with Filosa. Joly has talked of an "aggressive package" to stop the sale ([ad-hoc-news](https://ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/stellantis-stock-faces-friday-talks-over-brampton-plant-sale/70530426), [CP24](https://www.cp24.com/local/peel/2026/11/13/can-sale-of-stellantis-plant-in-brampton-be-stopped-ontario-cabinet-minister-hopes-meeting-with-ceo-could-buy-some-time/)). One report put the CEO meeting on Friday, Nov 20. Another source could not confirm a date. Treat it as unconfirmed. The likely cost is a few hundred million dollars, small against a market cap of about $13B, so this is more headline risk than a thesis changer.
- **Italy supply.** A shortage of an engine control unit has halted Fiat 500 output at Mirafiori into a fifth week, and Pomigliano (Panda) is also hit. Stellantis said stoppages could run through November and December. An unconfirmed press report says the 500 might restart only from Nov 23 to Dec 4. Unions doubt the parts explanation and point to weak demand ([TimesLIVE](https://www.timeslive.co.za/motoring/2026-11-12-parts-supply-issues-extend-fiat-500-plant-shutdown-into-fifth-week/)). That is a Q4 volume headwind.
- **Trade.** Stellantis is among the automakers most exposed to the North American trade-pact review. Several Ram and Jeep Cherokee models are built in Mexico. I found no outcome, and the sources I found were older.
- **Credit.** S&P rates it BBB-, one notch above junk, with a negative outlook (per 24/7 Wall St). Securities class-action suits over the EV strategy are pending.
- **Breakup talk.** RBC called a breakup "a plausible longer-term scenario."

## What a bounce would need
- A constructive Canada outcome, such as a negotiated package or a smaller repayment.
- Strong Ram and Jeep US sales, with Q4 sales reported in early January.
- Evidence that chip and commodity inflation is smaller than feared.
- Simple oversold mean reversion (RSI 28, a 3.7 ATR stretch).

## What would extend the slide
- More downgrades. Oddo's €3 target is within about 8% of the current price.
- Escalation in Canada.
- More Italian shutdowns.
- Credit-rating action.
- Any sign of an equity raise.

I did not find a scheduled company event before the Dec 12 Canada deadline. Full-year results should come in February (my expectation, not a date I found).

## Caveats
- Several sources are AI-assisted aggregators (MarketBeat, ad-hoc-news, Defense World). Prices mix euros and dollars, and the dollar/euro relationship here is roughly 1.08.
- I did not confirm Brampton or Friday-meeting details against primary Canadian government releases.

**The story: why it sold off**

  - Distribution costs are rising. The net reserve margin fell to 37.8% on the Hyperliquid deal and should step down again in Q4 with the renewed Binance deal.
  - RLDC margin (revenue less distribution costs) was 39.7% excluding the presale.
  - Adjusted opex is trending toward the high end of the $570–585M guide.
  - Management reaffirmed its 40% through-cycle USDC growth target but said growth "will not follow a straight line". It gave no October or November circulation figures.
  - A 5% workforce cut took place in the quarter.
- **Stock reaction:** The stock fell about 12% the next day, its worst session since June (Stocktwits, TIKR). It fell another 5% on 11/17, a two-day slide of about 12%. Mizuho called the quarter "uneventful".
- **Analyst split:**

  - Bulls: JPMorgan Overweight at $100 (cut from $110), TD Cowen Buy at $87 (cut from $92), Bernstein Buy at $145.

**HGV research as of 7:45 PM CT, Wed 2026-11-18**

I found no news item dated Nov 17–18 that explains today's 2.3% move. I searched for one and came up empty. The page-reading tool was blocked (403) on a few sources, so some items below come from search summaries only.

**The story in one line.** HGV is a timeshare company that cut its 2026 guidance after a weak Q3. The stock has still rallied about 30% off its low, helped by a large buyback and an activist holder, and heavy short covering looks like a big part of it.

**Q3 results (reported Oct 29, company release)**
- Contract sales were $807M, down 11%. Volume per guest (VPG, sales per tour) fell 12% to about $3,400. Tours rose 2%, so the problem was closing sales, not traffic.
- 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance (excluding deferrals and recognitions) was cut to $1.165–1.180B, from $1.225–1.265B.
- Management says the shortfall came from weak closing rates, especially at Bluegreen sales sites. It blamed incentive design, recruiting and staff turnover.
- The fix so far: leadership replaced at some sites, new incentive plans, and more than 430 experienced salespeople hired, including 165 former HGV reps. Mike Riley was named Chief Sales & Marketing Officer.
- Management said sales bottomed in August and improved in September and October. For Q4 it guides contract sales down low to mid single digits and VPG down mid single digits.
- The headline numbers are flattered:
  - The reported $3.70 EPS and $609M EBITDA include a $296M net benefit from recognizing previously deferred revenue on the Ka Haku (Waikiki) project.
  - The credit-loss provision fell to 12.5% of owned contract sales. A methodology change drove that, with a $55M estimate change. Under the old method it would have been about 20%. Management expects the mid-teens going forward.
- Balance sheet: net leverage was 3.87x, with $684M of liquidity.

**Buyback**
- HGV repurchased $110M of stock in Q3 and still targets $600M for the full year.
- On Oct 30 it announced a $200M accelerated repurchase with Deutsche Bank, about 4.48M shares at $35.71. It settles by Dec 31, and Deutsche can end it early from Dec 1.
- $417M remains authorized after that. The company-wide $617M figure was as of Oct 22.

**Activist**
- CAS Investment Partners (Cliff Sosin) filed a 13D on Aug 14 for 6.5% of the shares (5.07M). The filing says it is discussing board seats, strategy, capital allocation and governance.
- I found no settlement, nomination or board seat as of today.
- CAS's Q3 13F was due around Nov 14. I did not find it.

**Insiders, shorts and analysts**
- CEO Mark Wang bought 12,200 shares on Nov 2 at $40.92, about $0.5M.
- Another executive, Charles Corbin Jr., sold 60,401 shares on Nov 4 at $43.41 under a pre-arranged selling plan.
- Short interest was 13.9M shares as of Oct 30, about 19% of shares outstanding. It was up 82% in two weeks, with days to cover around 11. Short covering plausibly fed the rally.
- Citi and Citizens JMP downgraded to neutral on Nov 2. Targets were cut by Barclays (to $39), Goldman (to $35) and JPMorgan (to $38). The consensus target is about $49.10 (2 Buy, 10 Hold, 1 Sell). Those targets sit below today's price of $46.45.

**Peers**
- Marriott Vacations (VAC) reported Q3 on Nov 4 with contract sales up 29% and VPG up 30%, and raised its full-year guide. That makes HGV's miss look company-specific, not an industry slump.
- I did not find Travel + Leisure (TNL) results.

**Price context**
- The stock closed at $35.71 on Oct 29, jumped about 7.7% after earnings, and reached about $41 by Nov 2–3. It was around $44 by Nov 14 and closed at $46.45 today.
- The 52-week range is $33.99 to $55.40, and the market cap is about $3.3B.
- Beta is 1.6.

  - The buyback is large and has a defined end date.
  - Management is saying sales are improving.
  - An activist is involved.
  - The stock is breaking out on 1.9x volume.

- On Nov 17 XLV fell 1.4% on a managed-care selloff. UNH fell 5.4%, all seven other managed-care names worth over $2B fell too (median -3.9%), and the S&P 500 fell 1.0% ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/unh/articles/626290/why-is-unitedhealth-stock-falling/2026-11-18)).
- On Nov 18 XLV was down about 2% intraday. Humana fell 10.6%, UNH 9.0% and Elevance 6.5% around 1:40 PM ET, two days after CMS proposed extending Medicare Advantage audit recoveries back to 2018 ([Quantisnow](https://quantisnow.com/articles/cms-audit-proposal-drives-humana-unitedhealth-and-elevance-lower-as-s-p-500-edges-up)). Intraday XLV prices on the quote pages I found were inconsistent, so treat the exact figure as approximate.
- UNH is about 5% of XLV, and the sector's two-day drop is concentrated in insurers. Distributors are not insurers, so they held up. That is why the basket "outperformed" while MCK and CAH were slightly down.
- A 4.4% five-day and 4.5% twenty-day relative gain therefore partly reflects XLV weakness. Part of it is also the earnings-driven gains from Nov 4-5.

**Earnings, Nov 4-5 (all three beat; the market read them differently)**
- **MCK (fiscal Q2 2027, Nov 4):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $11.68, up 18%, against about $10.7 expected. Revenue was $110.96B.
  - FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $45.60-46.40 from $44.20-45.00.
  - GLP-1 distribution revenue was $16B, up 26%. Oncology and multispecialty revenue rose 24%, but its profit rose only 8% (23% excluding prior-year gains) ([Averin](https://averin.com/en/journal/ruslan-averin-cvs-cencora-mckesson-cardinal-humana-q3-2026-earnings-results-healthcare)).
  - It closed the Precision Medicine Group deal. It also agreed to take a 49% stake in Option Care Health for about $1.4B, expected to close in the first half of 2027 ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/mck/articles/626238/the-open-question-in-mckessons-two-new-deals/2026-11-18)).
- **COR (fiscal Q4 2026, Nov 4):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $4.66 against $4.56 expected.
  - FY27 EPS guidance of $19.40-19.75 has a midpoint below the Street's roughly $19.78-19.91.
  - Pharmaceutical Distribution is guided up only 2-4% on a customer volume shift and a currency headwind. GLP-1 added $2.8B of revenue, but manufacturer price cuts removed $2.8B.
  - The stock rose 4% on Nov 4, then fell 4.1% and 1.8% to $333.56, about 2% below its pre-report close.
  - It raised the dividend 10% to $0.66 (record date Nov 13, payable Nov 30).
  - Analysts still raised targets: Barclays to $415, JPMorgan to $413, Leerink to $405. The MWI Animal Health/Covetrus merger carries regulatory uncertainty ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/heres-why-retain-cencora-stock-112400911.html)).
- **CAH (fiscal Q1 2027, Nov 5):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $3.26, up 28%, against about $2.92 expected. Revenue was $67.5B.
  - FY27 guidance was raised to $12.80-13.00 from $12.40-12.60.
  - Pharma segment profit rose 17%, and specialty revenue grew 18%.
  - GLP-1 added about 5 points to revenue growth, and Inflation Reduction Act price cuts took off about 4 points.
  - It bought back $500M of stock in the quarter, and CVS renewed its contract.
  - Risks: the fastest-growing "Other" segment missed, and the medical products unit faces tariff and petroleum-cost pressure ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/investingclub/2026/11/05/were-raising-our-price-target-on-cardinal-health-after-another-stellar-quarter-of-profits.html)).
  - The CNBC Investing Club author noted some of the stock's gains reflect sector rotation rather than company-specific fundamentals, and trimmed the position into strength.

**Price levels**
- **MCK:** record close of $1,105.15 on Nov 16, the same day Jim Cramer said on air "get me into McKesson" ([247WallSt](https://247wallst.com/cards/mckesson-mck-enriched-price-move-01m7kc2a8swqpjevphxa1qna0b)). It opened Nov 18 at $1,088.68. The 1-year range is $723.68-1,121.50, the 50-day average is about $963 and the 200-day about $877. That puts it roughly 13% above its 50-day average, with a P/E near 28 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-mckesson-nyse-mck-stock-price-expected-to-rise-barclays-analyst-says-2026-11-18/)).
  - Barclays raised its target to $1,235 and JPMorgan to $1,255. The average target of about $1,054 is below the price.
  - One executive sold 650 shares on Nov 5 under a pre-arranged plan.
- **CAH:** opened Nov 18 at $279.29, with a 12-month high of $286.29, so it sits near its high. Barclays raised its target to $320, Wells Fargo to $321, Argus to $309 and RBC to $295. The consensus target of about $287-290 is roughly at the price ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-barclays-forecasts-strong-price-appreciation-for-cardinal-health-nyse-cah-stock-2026-11-18/)).
- **COR:** about $334-350 in the sources I found. It is the laggard, 5-10% below its Nov 4 high.

**Background story**
- All three are riding GLP-1 volume, specialty and oncology growth, buybacks and low-beta defensiveness. Some commentary credits rotation out of AI-linked stocks. The earlier sources I found cover late 2025, so that rotation point is weakly supported for now.
- Margins are thin. GLP-1 revenue is large but low-profit, and Cencora says profitability on it is modest and not expected to improve soon. Brand price cuts, including IRA cuts, erode revenue growth.
- Pharma tariffs (a Section 232 tariff of up to 100% since Jul 31, 2026) exempt generics and companies with Most Favored Nation pricing deals. A generic-drug tariff is planned from 2028 with a two-year delay. I found no distributor-specific analysis of tariff or Most Favored Nation exposure.
- CVS is a major customer and plans a 2028 spin-off. Cardinal says its CVS service will continue beyond it.

**Upcoming events**
- No earnings fall inside the one-to-ten-session window. MCK reports fiscal Q3 around February 2027, and CAH and COR also report in early February. I did not find confirmed dates for Cardinal or Cencora.
- Only the J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference (Jan 11-14, 2027) is listed as upcoming for Cencora. McKesson presented at the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference on Nov 17 and has an ASHP Midyear focus coming.
- I found no scheduled catalyst in the window. The main swing factors are the managed-care and Medicare policy news flow driving XLV, and any pullback in the extended names.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **For:** the earnings beats and raised guidance are real, the targets are rising, and the defensive bid is intact.
- **Against:** MCK and CAH are at or near records and above or at consensus targets. The relative move relies on XLV falling, which can reverse if insurers bounce. Cramer's mention may have marked a short-term sentiment peak.
- COR is the cleanest "catch-up" candidate but has a below-consensus outlook.

**Gaps:** I found no verified Nov 17 or Nov 18 closing prices, no distributor-specific news for those days, and no confirmed fiscal Q2 earnings dates for CAH and COR. Searches had mostly stopped surfacing new material by the end.

**PATH research brief, as of 7:45 PM CT Wed 2026-11-18**

**Bottom line:** I found no hard company-specific news behind today's 5.3% drop. The one dated catalyst is a Cleveland Research note that raised ARR risk for FY28 (fiscal year ending Jan 2028). The rest is a slow slide on AI-pricing doubts and fears that AI agents will displace UiPath. Nothing I found suggests a rebound catalyst before the 12/3 earnings report.

**Price context (stockanalysis.com)**
- PATH closed at $11.73 (-5.33%) and traded $11.80 after hours.
- Market cap is about $6.1B.
- The analyst consensus is Hold from 20 analysts, with a mean target of $15.41.
- Nov 17 was also a weak market day: S&P 500 -1.0%, Dow -1.65%, Nasdaq -0.7%. PATH fell 5.7% that day to $12.39, which is the "20-day low" the screen references.

**What drove the recent selling**
- **Nov 18:** Cleveland Research said it sees downside risk to FY28 ARR. It argues competition and AI-related budget shifts could displace UiPath's business and make FY28 "challenging." Shares were down nearly 3% early in the session. UiPath had not commented, and I found no quantified downside case. Only short summaries were available (Seeking Alpha via TradingView, TokenPost). The GuruFocus page returned a 403.
- **Sept 4:** Q2 results on Sept 3 beat guidance, but the stock sold off hard. Zacks attributed this to a Q3 revenue midpoint below consensus and a small ARR raise (+0.3%). One earlier search result put the Sept 4 drop at 16.6% in a day, and I didn't confirm it independently.
- **Late September:** DA Davidson (Lucky Schreiner) downgraded PATH to Underperform and cut its target to $10 from $16, after the FUSION conference and Investor Day. The reason was "significant resistance to the company's AI pricing structure" in customer and partner feedback.
  - UBS cut to $15 on about Sept 22, then to $14, and doubts Coding Agents lift ARR growth well above about 10% by FY28.
  - RBC cut to $15 and calls it a "show-me story."
  - TD Cowen and BMO both cut to $15, and Canaccord to $14 (Hold).
  - Barron's called September the stock's worst month in four years.
- **October 16:** The stock fell about 7% intraday on reports of slowing automation demand and cautious enterprise spending. It had been trading between about $12.20 and $13.80.
- **Earlier in 2026:** There were repeated AI-disruption sell-offs, for example on AWS agent news in April and on Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents. These come from aggregator sites, so treat them as lower confidence.
- **Correction to a search summary:** One search summary said DA Davidson downgraded on Nov 16. The sources I opened date it to late September, so ignore the Nov 16 claim.

**Fundamentals (Q2 FY27, quarter ended July 31; company press release and call summary)**
- Revenue was $410.3M, up 13% (16% in constant currency).
- ARR was $1.938B, up 12%, with only $37M of net new ARR. Cloud ARR is above $1.3B, up more than 19%.
- Dollar-based net retention was 109% and gross retention 97%.
- Customers with $1M+ ARR grew 21% to 387, and they account for about 50% of revenue.
- Non-GAAP operating margin was 22% and GAAP operating income was $31.6M. Stock-based compensation fell 42% to $45M.
- Adjusted free cash flow was $31M, down from $45M, partly on tax-payment timing.
- Cash and securities are $1.4B with no debt. UiPath repurchased $268.5M of stock in the first half, and the Q2 shares were bought at an average of $9.63, below today's price.
- Guidance for Q3 FY27:
  - Revenue of $440-445M.
  - ARR of $1.992-1.997B, which implies about $54-59M of net new ARR, a step up from Q2's $37M.
  - Non-GAAP operating income of about $100M.
- Full-year FY27 guidance:
  - Revenue of $1.789-1.794B.
  - ARR of $2.065-2.070B.
  - Operating income of about $445M.
  - Free cash flow of about $425M.
- FX is a headwind of about $10M to Q3 revenue.
- Management: 18 of its top 20 deals included AI. New products are Maestro, Coding Agents and an agentic workflow tool. Coding Agents are still "proving stage."
- Leadership: Hitesh Ramani became CFO, and Ashim Gupta stays as COO.
- Management gave no preliminary FY28 ARR guidance. UBS read that as comfort with Street estimates of about 10% ARR growth.

**Earnings and consensus**
- UiPath's own release confirms Q3 FY27 results on Thursday, Dec 3, after the close, with a call at 5:00 PM ET (4:00 PM CT). That is 11 sessions from tomorrow, so the earnings gap falls outside the 1-10 session window. One calendar shows a projected Dec 8 date, but that is an estimate and the company's date is the one to rely on.
- Zacks consensus for Q3 is EPS $0.19 and revenue of about $442.7M. Forward P/E is about 16.6 and the Zacks Rank is #3 (Hold).

**Positioning**
- Short interest was 25.56% of float as of Aug 31, per a Yahoo/Insider Monkey piece. A different source quoted 38% in June, with the year unclear. I couldn't find a current figure.
- Hedge fund holders rose to 48 at the end of Q2 from 40 in Q1.
- I found no recent insider buying. The CEO sold 45,000-share blocks in late 2025 and early Jan 2026 at about $15.7-16.5.

**Minor news (not price-relevant)**
- Nov 10: named a Google Cloud Gemini for healthcare launch partner.
- Nov 5: named a Leader in Everest Group's agentic process automation assessment.
- Oct 9: named a Leader in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for agentic QA.
- Sept 30: Snowflake integration.

**For the 1-10 session trade decision**
- **Bearish:** The stock has broken below its 20-day low and the 200-day average on 1.8x volume. The narrative is still negative and analysts are cutting. A new third-party warning landed today, and it's unclear whether the market has fully priced it.
- **Bullish or mean-reversion:** The stock is oversold (RSI 31), 31% below the mean target, and valuation is modest at about 16.6x forward earnings. It has cash, buybacks (average cost $9.63) and heavy short interest (stale data), which can produce sharp squeezes. Q3 guidance implies a net new ARR rebound, so some pre-earnings positioning toward Dec 3 is plausible.
- **Gaps:** I couldn't find what drove the Nov 17 close beyond the weak market, and I couldn't read the Cleveland Research note itself. I found no UiPath response and no news after the close on Nov 18 beyond the after-hours uptick.

agents.report:
**GLBE after the Q3 2026 report (Nov 18, 2026): research summary**

**Bottom line:** This was a clean beat and raise that the stock sold on. Growth slowed, gross margin fell, and the stock had run up into the print. Intraday weakness faded, with the close in the top third of the range on 5.3 times normal volume. That could be absorption of selling, but nothing I found shows who bought. Fundamentals and sell-side targets sit well above the price. A near-term catalyst to force a re-rating is thin: the holiday read-through is the main one, and the 2027 duty-drawback ramp comes later.

**What was reported**
- **Revenue:** $314.1M, up 42%. This is the top of the $308.5–315.5M guide, but only about 0.5% above the $312.6M consensus.
- **GMV:** $2,042M, up 35%. This is the top of the guide and slightly above the $2,032M consensus.
  - Q2 GMV was $2.09B, up 44%. So Q3 fell sequentially and growth slowed about 9 points. Management said Q3 is normally 1–2% above Q2, but Q2 had concentrated promotions.
- **Adjusted EBITDA:** $63.7M (20.3% margin, up from 18.7%). This beat the $58.5–62.5M guide and the roughly $61M consensus.
- **Non-GAAP EPS:** $0.37 against $0.23 consensus. The beat is mostly noise from pre-print estimates sitting low. GAAP EPS was $0.47, helped by a $49M tax valuation-allowance release.
- **Non-GAAP gross margin:** 44.8%, down from 46.3%. Adjusted gross profit was $140.6M against about $142M expected, a slight miss.
- **Free cash flow:** $66.4M, down from $73.6M a year earlier.
- **Mix:** Fulfillment revenue grew 54% and service fees grew 30%.

**Guidance**
- **Full year 2026 (raised):**

| Metric | New | Prior |
|---|---|---|
| GMV | $8.957–9.117B | $8.81–9.11B |
| Revenue | $1.329–1.353B | $1.305–1.355B |
| Adjusted EBITDA | $290–300M | $278–300M |

- The low ends rose more than the high ends, so the raise is partly narrowing.
- **Q4 2026 (first time given):**
  - GMV $3.085–3.245B, about 34% growth.
  - Revenue $464–488M.
  - Adjusted EBITDA $113.5–123.5M, about a 24.9% margin.
  - Truist says the midpoint was in line with consensus. I found no hard Q4 consensus figures.
- **Same-store sales:** Management said these slowed from the first half. It cited FX and promotions and says this is in the Q4 guide. Holiday promotions started earlier, and management says peak demand is still ahead.
- **2027:** No formal guide. Management expects "another strong year" within its March Investor Day framework.

**Why it sold off**
- **Gross margin:** The decline came from lower-margin Passport and a fuel-surcharge pause. Passport's EBITDA margin is below the company average. The fuel surcharge was updated toward Q4, which management expects to show in results.
- **Passport mix:** Fulfillment was a bigger share of Passport revenue than planned, and its service-fee revenue came in below expectations.
- **Take rates:** Service-fee take rates are falling. Causes are the Shopify Managed Markets V1-to-V2 migration and volume tiers for larger merchants. Management expects them to be "quite stable" from here.
- **Passport inflates growth:** A Nov 10 preview put underlying 2026 growth at about 32% excluding Passport.
- **Expectations:** A Nov 10 preview had consensus revenue near the top of the guide, and the stock sat near its $45.28 high.
- **Reaction path:**
  - The prior close was $39.81.
  - Premarket was down 12–14%, to about $34–35.
  - An Investing.com piece cited $37.12 (down 6.8%) at one point.
  - Your screen shows a close of $38.03, down 4.5%.

**Story pieces**
- **Shopify Managed Markets 2.0:** Volumes accelerated through Q3, and GMV growth outpaced the core business in the back half of the quarter.
  - Managed pricing with guaranteed shipping lifted conversion by about 50% for merchants using it.
  - The UK and Canada doubled their share of daily volume.
  - Shopify's "Global by Default" is rolling out to some new merchants.
- **Passport:** Acquired this year for about $178.8M in Q3 payments. It is integrated and in line with the forecast. Further synergies are planned for 2027.
- **Duty drawback:**
  - US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) approved reclaims on returned goods. First claims are expected before year-end, and management estimates about 2% of cost of trade saved for non-US sellers.
  - The J1 program is slower than expected because of a backlog from the Supreme Court's IEEPA tariff ruling. Management expects it to pick up in early 2027.
- **Agentic commerce:** AI-sourced checkouts roughly doubled quarter over quarter but are still a very small share.
- **Retention:** Attrition is under 4%. Net dollar retention was over 120% in the first half.
- **Capital:** $53M of buybacks in Q3, with about $446M left on a $500M plan. Cash and investments are $347M.
- **New logos:** Many enterprise launches, including Acqua di Parma, Balmain, Pangaia and COSRX. The base is over 1,500 brands.

**Street and valuation**
- **Analysts:** All 13 covering analysts rated it Buy before the print, with a consensus target of about $51.
- **Post-print targets:**
  - BMO raised its target to $51 from $48.
  - Truist reiterated Buy at $48.
  - A search summary also reported a Morgan Stanley upgrade to Overweight with a $50 target. I could not verify it. The only upgrade I found was dated 2025, so treat it as unconfirmed.
- **Valuation:** Market cap is about $6.7B and the P/E is about 45 on GAAP.

**History and pattern**
- GLBE has repeatedly sold off on strong prints with a raise:
  - Feb 2024: down about 17%.
  - Feb 2025: down about 25% over a week.
  - Aug 2025: down despite a raise.
  - Nov 2025: down 5.1%.
- It rose after the Q2 2026 print, trading around $43. Before this print it was about $42, then $39.81 on the last close.

**For the 1–10 session decision**
- **For a long:**
  - A reversal close against the gap on heavy volume.
  - Price above the 200-day average (35.96).
  - A real beat and raise, with the stock about 25% below targets.
  - Black Friday and Cyber Monday data in the window.
  - Possible early duty-drawback claim news before year-end.
- **Against:**
  - Price is below the 50-day average (40.32), and the pre-print level near $40 is overhead resistance.
  - Gross-margin and take-rate concerns are not resolved, and growth is slowing.
  - There is no further scheduled company catalyst.
  - There is a pattern of drifting lower after earnings.
  - The $34–35 premarket low is the key level.
- **Unknowns I could not find:** short interest, options positioning, and any post-print analyst cuts. I also could not confirm the Morgan Stanley item or a Q4 consensus.

**ARMK: research summary for the 1–10 session decision (as of 7:45 PM CT, Nov 18, 2026)**

**Bottom line:** The bad news was mostly one-off cost, the sell-off was already bought, and the buyback and Nexus growth story are real. **BIDU research, 2026-11-18, 7:45 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** The story is a core ad business in decline, a growing but lower-margin AI cloud business, and falling profit estimates. A tail of sector and policy news sits on top of that. The stock is oversold (RSI 26) and below its prior 52-week low. I found no catalyst inside one to ten sessions that is Baidu-specific and clearly positive. The nearest swing event is Alibaba's earnings on Thursday.

**What the quarter showed (Q3 2026, reported 11/16)**
- The SEC 6-K shows revenue of RMB 30.8B, down 1% year over year and down 2% from the prior quarter. That is the sixth straight quarter of falling total revenue.
- General business revenue was RMB 25.0B, up 1%, the first year-over-year rise in the period.
- Online marketing (ads) was RMB 11.9B, down 22%.
- Management blamed macro conditions, competition, and a deliberate choice to put user experience ahead of monetization in AI Search.
- AI-native marketing services were RMB 2.4B, down 15%.
- AI Cloud Infra was RMB 8.2B, up 94% (it was up 50% the quarter before). GPU Cloud was up 191%.
- Core AI-powered revenue was RMB 13.2B, up 37%, or 53% of general business.
- iQIYI was RMB 6.0B, down 10%.
- Non-GAAP operating margin was 6% (RMB 1.7B), versus 7% a year ago. GAAP operating income was only RMB 626M.
- Non-GAAP EPS was RMB 6.78 per ADS (about $1.01) versus $1.66 a year ago.
- Capex was RMB 7.3B against operating cash flow of RMB 2.8B, so free cash flow was about negative RMB 4.6B.
- Cash and investments were RMB 276.6B (about $41B).
- Buybacks total only $373M year to date.
- A first cash dividend is "expected before year-end", subject to board approval.
- There was no numeric guidance. The call said ads stay "under considerable pressure" and profit is under pressure near term. AI Cloud is expected to take over as the profit driver over time.
- Q3 capex was RMB 4B below Q2, and management says it will pace spending to customer demand and cash collection.
- Reports on the call say the CEO warned that AI spending must produce tangible profit to avoid a "bubble" outcome.

**Conflict with your screen:** Your screen shows a +10% EPS surprise, but sources disagree on whether Q3 beat or missed.
- Investing.com and Benzinga say adjusted EPS of 6.78 missed an 8.16 consensus by about 17%. Investing.com's own transcript summary notes the currency is unclear.
- A Yahoo/Investing.com item says 6.78 yuan beat an LSEG consensus of 6.36 yuan. Stocktwits also says results beat.
- The 6.36 and 8.16 figures are on different consensus bases, so the "beat" is probably against a lower, fresher consensus.
- Estimates had already fallen about 24% in 30 days and 46% in 90 days before the print. That is consistent with "beat a lowered bar, still sold."
- Either way, the reaction is a sell on ad and margin quality, not on the headline number.

**Why the stock is falling**
- **Ad disintermediation:** Ads are the profit engine and they are shrinking 22%. A Seeking Alpha piece on 11/4 downgraded to Sell on AI "disintermediation" risk. Morgan Stanley went to Underweight in October with an $80 target.
- **Mix shift:** Aletheia says lower-margin GPU rental is replacing high-margin ads, which pressures margins.
- **Earlier history:** Q2 (reported 8/18) was already a bad print. One blogger (unverified, an opinion piece) says the stock fell 12.7% on 8.1x volume that day. He says AI cloud fell sequentially from RMB 8.8B to 7.3B, gross margin fell to 44.5%, and net profit fell 68%. The same source says the Apollo Go robotaxi ride count was dropped from the written Q2 release. He puts Q2 rides at about 1M versus 3.2M in Q1, and says Wuhan operations were suspended after a 3/31 incident.
- **Apollo Go in Q3:** The Q3 ride count was again not disclosed, and regulatory status was not discussed. Q3 facts: 30 cities, 34M autonomous kilometers, driverless rides in Shenzhen up about 170% from the prior quarter, Dubai fleet doubled, London testing with Uber and Lyft.
- **YTD:** The stock is down roughly 45% to 53% this year (sources disagree). It was about $162 in January.
- **Today's drivers (Stocktwits, 11/18):** The stock hit its lowest level since July 2010. HK shares hit a record low of HK$69.15 and the Hang Seng was down about 1%.

# LivaNova (LIVN) research, as of 7:45 PM CT, 2026-11-18

## Bottom line
LIVN is a profitable, steady-growth medtech with an earnings-driven re-rating. The stock rose from about $79.90 to about $91.14 on Nov 5, after Q3 results and a guidance raise. It has since held the high $80s to mid-$90s.

I found no company news that explains today's close at a new closing high. Treat the breakout as momentum and flow, not a new catalyst. Nothing scheduled falls inside a 1–10 session window. The next earnings are about Feb 24, 2027. The SNIA court hearing is Feb 10, 2027.

## The story
**Core business (about 98% of revenue)**
- **Q3 2026 results (reported Nov 4):**
  - Revenue was $393.1M, up 9.9% (consensus about $381M).
  - Adjusted EPS was $1.23 (consensus about $1.06–1.08).
  - Adjusted operating margin was 23.5%.
- **Cardiopulmonary:** $225M, up 10.9%.
  - Heart-lung machines grew low double digits on record placements of the newer Essenz model, with favorable price and mix.
  - Oxygenator share rose from about 30% to about 40% over two years.
  - The company says it is capacity-constrained and on backorder. One of four major competitors has exited the market.
  - A new dedicated production line is running. Output gains arrive in early 2027, with double-digit output growth guided for 2027.
- **Epilepsy (vagus nerve stimulation):** about +11%.
  - Realized price is running at about twice the normal annual increase.
  - Medicare reimbursement is up about 50%, and CMS confirmed the same new-patient rate for 2027.
  - A new digitally enabled device launches in 2027, the first new epilepsy device in eight years.
  - The CORE-VNS 36-month data showed a 76% median seizure reduction.
- **FY2026 guidance, raised:**

| Item | New | Prior |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue growth (constant currency) | 9–10% | 8–9% |
| Adjusted EPS | $4.40–4.50 | $4.30–4.40 |
| Adjusted free cash flow | $140–160M | unchanged |

  - Adjusted operating margin is 20–21%, unchanged.
  - Management says this puts 2026 at or above the 2025–2028 Investor Day framework.
  - There is no 2027 guidance yet.

**Growth options (not in the numbers yet)**
- **Sleep apnea (aura6000):**
  - The FDA approved the device in March 2026.
  - It has no complete-concentric-collapse contraindication, which covers roughly 25–30% of patients. It also needs no sleep endoscopy before implant.
  - The current device is not yet on the US market. The next-generation version needs an FDA supplement, expected to be filed between late 2026 and the first half of 2027.
  - Limited launch is in 2027, with meaningful spending in 2028.
  - New CPT billing codes (Category I) take effect Jan 1, 2028.
  - The target is $200–400M of revenue by 2030.
  - A supplement filing announcement could land in the window. The timing is vague, so it is a possible upside headline, not a scheduled one.
- **Depression:**
  - The 36-month RECOVER data went to CMS and a journal.
  - The company is in "active dialogue" with CMS and gave no timeline.
  - Management treats it as pure optionality, excluded from the plan.
  - I found no CMS decision.

**Sector read-through**
- Inspire Medical, the leader in this market, saw Q3 revenue fall 7.9%. It blames coding and reimbursement confusion and expects about $120M of impact in 2026. It also got a new code effective 2028.
- Nyxoah's US Genio launch is ramping, but it cut its 2026 guidance.
- Together these say the sleep-apnea market is soft until 2028 and getting crowded. LivaNova's launch is therefore a long-dated story.

## Analysts and positioning
- **Price targets raised after Q3, ratings unchanged:**
  - Needham $112 (Buy).
  - Baird $111 (Outperform).
  - Mizuho $115.
  - Jefferies $120 (Buy).
  - Barclays $120 (Overweight, Nov 9).
- Consensus is Moderate Buy. The average target is about $101–105, with a range of $75–120.
- The stock is at about $94.5, near the consensus average. The Street's highest targets sit about 27% above.
- **Valuation:** about 20.6x 2026 EPS. EPS estimates are $4.43 for 2026, $4.73 for 2027 and $5.18 for 2028. One article's fair-value estimate was $92.36.
- **Short interest:** about 5.0M shares, 9.1% of float, 9 days to cover, rising slightly. This comes from a September figure, so it is stale. A squeeze could add fuel on breakouts.
- **Insiders:**
  - The CFO sold 2,500 shares at about $90.91 on Nov 12.
  - A director sold in September, and another executive sold $876K in August.
  - I found 8 insider sells and no buys over the past year.
  - This is mild and probably routine.
- Institutions own about 98%. I found no activist, takeover or buyback news.

## Risks and overhangs
1. **SNIA environmental liability (Italy):**
   - The 10-Q (quarterly filing) carries a current liability of €337.8M ($383.6M) as of Sep 30.
   - The Milan appeals court moved the hearing from Dec 9, 2026 to Feb 10, 2027. Settlement talks are ongoing. A higher damages award is possible.
   - On the call, management reportedly said a payment of about $400M shifted into Q4. The 10-Q gave no payment date, so I could not verify that. Cash is $563M and debt is $299M, so it looks fundable.
   - Any headline on this, either direction, could move the stock.
2. **3T heater-cooler litigation:**
   - The provision rose to $44.2M, with a $34M charge in Q3. That is why GAAP EPS was only $0.11.
   - About 55 claims remain.
3. **Q4 setup:**
   - Management flagged tough Q4 comparisons and a step-up in spending on sleep apnea, capacity and oxygenators.
   - One source says Q4 EPS is expected to be about 4.5% below last year. Nine analysts cut estimates in the past 90 days.
   - Free cash flow guidance did not rise. Q3 free cash flow was $56M versus $62M a year ago.
4. **Lumpy 2027 setup:** Essenz conversion nears 100%, so the price/mix tailwind fades after 2027. Epilepsy pricing and the near-term sleep apnea market also look soft.
5. **Convertible notes:** $345M of 2.5% notes at a $69.40 conversion price. The conversion trigger is $90.22 for 20 of 30 trading days. The stock is above it, and the notes could become convertible, which brings dilution and hedging flows, but only later (not in Q4).
6. **Tariffs:** under $5M of operating income impact.

agents.report:
**JD (JD.com) research summary, as of the evening of 2026-11-18.** The Q3 numbers are confirmed by primary sources. Several analyst and reaction details are only secondhand or conflicting. Several searches returned only 2025 or early-2026 material and added nothing new. I did not find the post-earnings analyst target changes.

## What happened on 11-17
- **Headline results (Q3 2026):** revenue was RMB 309.6B, up 3.5%. That compares with the LSEG average estimate of RMB 311.48B, so it was a small miss.
- **Profit versus consensus:** non-GAAP net profit was RMB 8.3B, up 44% year over year, against an estimate of RMB 8.59B. TipRanks says this ended eight straight quarters of beating EPS. Investing.com calls adjusted EPS "in line," so sources disagree on the size of the miss.
- **Operating income:** GAAP operating income was RMB 5.2B, versus a RMB 1.1B loss a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin was 2.4%, versus 0.1%.
- **JD Retail:** revenue was RMB 258B, up 2.9%. Operating income was RMB 15.1B, a 5.8% margin versus 5.9% a year earlier, so the margin slipped slightly. Gross margin was a record 20.1%, the 18th straight quarter of improvement.
- **JD Logistics:** revenue was RMB 64B, up 16.1%. Operating income was RMB 1.9B, up about 50%.
- **New Businesses (includes food delivery):** the operating loss narrowed to RMB 9.6B from RMB 15.7B. Revenue fell about 50%, partly because on-demand delivery was reclassified. The nine-month loss was RMB 29.8B.
- **Food delivery:** management gave no revenue, loss or order figures and no breakeven date. It said losses fell by more than half year over year and narrowed sequentially. It guided to a "significant" year-over-year cut in food delivery investment in 2027.
- **Where the profit gain came from:** marketing expense fell 26.2% to RMB 15.5B, mainly from lower food delivery subsidies. Investing.com argues the gain came from spending cuts rather than stronger sales, and that it depends on rivals easing discounting.
- **Cost pressure:** R&D rose 37%, which is AI and robotics spending. Management said it "may pressure short-term margins."
- **Weak spots:** electronics and appliances revenue fell 0.7%, which management tied to soft demand and subsidy pull-forward.
- **Cash flow:** Q3 operating cash flow was negative RMB 18.7B, versus negative RMB 8.0B a year earlier. Free cash flow was negative RMB 23.9B. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow is still about RMB 18.8B, and cash and short-term investments are RMB 214.7B.
- **Guidance:** none was given. Management only said JD Retail is working toward "healthy high single-digit" operating margins over time.
- **Buyback:** the $5B program runs through August 2027. About $1.0B was left as of June 30, and the Q3 release does not mention it.
- **Ceconomy (MediaMarkt/Saturn owner):** JD closed the takeover on Nov 12, buying 59.8% for EUR 1.335B in cash. With Convergenta's 25.3% stake, JD's holding reaches 85.2%, and JD is weighing a delisting. Bears call it an expensive European purchase during cautious consumer spending.

## Why the stock fell
- Investing.com's hypothesis, which I'd treat as reasoning rather than sourced fact, is that revenue and profit were slightly light, the retail margin slipped, and cash flow was sharply negative. It also cites an unresolved food delivery path, subsidy uncertainty and a weak consumer backdrop.
- Consensus EPS was cut 9.6% over 60 days and 21% over a year. There were 14 downward revisions versus one upward before the report.
- Instant retail share was estimated at only about 7.7%, versus roughly 45% each for Taobao Instant Commerce and Meituan. That makes the food delivery spending hard to justify.
- China's October retail sales rose just 0.4% year over year, against a forecast of 1.07%, with a property slowdown weighing on consumers.
- Alibaba shares also fell in sympathy on Nov 17.
- Management flagged uncertainty over 2027 national trade-in subsidies. The 2026 trade-in bond allocation was cut to RMB 250B, and Caixin describes the program as fading. I found no official 2027 budget.

## Sentiment and valuation
- Per TipRanks, ratings are 6 Buy, 1 Hold and 1 Sell, with an average target of $37.40 (high $48). That is about 35% above the price.
- Simply Wall St's fair value is about $39. It puts the stock down 13.9% year to date and down 67.6% over five years.
- FY2026 EPS consensus is RMB 21.13, rising to RMB 26.96 in FY2027, so Investing.com notes much of the recovery is already assumed. Next-quarter consensus is EPS of RMB 4.29 on revenue of RMB 369.9B.
- Morgan Stanley was Underweight with a $24 target as of January. Bernstein was Outperform at $38 as of November 2025. Neither is a post-earnings update.
- Benzinga ran a headline that analysts slashed forecasts after Q3, but I could not open the page, so I have no firm names or numbers.

## Catalysts and risks for the next 1-10 sessions
- **Alibaba earnings (Thursday, per Benzinga headline):** this is the nearest read-through on quick-commerce and food delivery losses. I could not open the page or confirm the exact time. Meituan reports Q3 later, probably in late November. I could not confirm a date.
- **Analyst target cuts:** more cuts are likely to follow the print, which could keep the stock under pressure.
- **Technical level:** Investing.com cites a 52-week low of $24.51, while your screen says $23.66. Reconcile the two figures before using that level.
- **Subsidies and competition:** any renewed food delivery or discounting escalation would hurt JD.
- **Policy:** any China stimulus or consumption support would help, and so would a 2027 subsidy announcement.
- **Mixed picture:** the bull case is a stock near its low with record gross margin, falling losses, net cash and buybacks. The bear case is 3.5% growth, falling estimates, negative cash flow and heavy AI and overseas spending.

## Data caveats
- I could not find the Reuters story or any JD price move for Nov 18. Yahoo's "up almost 8%" comes from a tool-generated article, so treat it loosely.
- A TipRanks line giving 22.6% or 23% profit growth conflicts with the SEC release. I used the SEC figures.

**Bottom line:** I found no news item dated November 18 for any of the four names, and no dated market wrap for the group or XLV. I could not find what drove today's +3.2% basket move. The most plausible read is a sector or tape move with no single catalyst, but that is inference, not something I confirmed. The four names have different stories, so the basket is a loose grouping. Almost all the news is 2 to 6 weeks old, and the main earnings events are already priced in.

**HSIC (best today, +3.3%)**
- **Q3 (reported Nov 3):** Sales were $3.47B, up 4.0%, with organic growth of 3.1%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.56. Excluding a $0.19 one-time tariff refund (a $28M benefit in cost of goods sold), EPS was $1.37, up 19% year over year.
- **Segments:** US dental merchandise rose 8.6%, mostly on volume, with share gains from private practices and dental service organizations (DSOs). Medical distribution grew only 1.1%, held back by weak point-of-care diagnostics and vaccine sales. Management expects a stronger flu season in Q4 to help. Value-added services fell 4.8%.
- **Stock reaction:** The stock fell 4.8% on Nov 3, its worst day of the year, from about $86.6 to $82.5. It closed at $88.74 on Nov 10, so it has recovered. Evercore raised its target to $90 on Nov 5.
- **Guidance:** The EPS guide was raised to $5.50–5.56, with the raise including the tariff refund.
- **Nov 16 reporting change:** The guide was then lowered to $5.42–5.48. This is a reporting change, not a weaker outlook. It excludes acquisition remeasurement gains from non-GAAP EPS, which removes $0.08.
- **Buybacks:** The company bought back $125M in Q3 and has about $330M left. CFO Emmanuel Caprais was named in October.
- **Next events:** The Jefferies conference was Nov 17, and Piper Sandler is Dec 1. Q4 earnings are Feb 23, 2027.
- **Risks:** Discretionary dental demand, diagnostics volatility, and Brazil.

**ALGN**
- **Q3 (reported around Oct 28):** Revenue was $1.015B, up 1.9%. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.80 against $2.77 expected. Clear aligner shipments were 690.6k, up 6.6%, and flat from Q2. North America orthodontist shipments grew year over year for the first time in six quarters, and DSO shipments rose double digits. Systems and Services revenue fell 7.6%.
- **Guidance:** The 2026 revenue guide was trimmed to $4.11–4.13B, the low end of the prior range, on mix and foreign exchange. Non-GAAP operating margin of about 23.7% was kept. Shares slipped after the report.
- **CEO change:** Jennifer Davis, formerly CEO of P&G's global healthcare business, became CEO-elect on Nov 2 and takes over as CEO on Dec 31. Joe Hogan retires from the board in June 2027. Detailed 2027 guidance was deferred to the next report under the new CEO.
- **Buyback:** A $270M accelerated repurchase was announced Nov 6 and runs to about Dec 29, which brings 2026 repurchases to about $500M. About $330M remains on the program. This is a steady bid under the stock.
- **Risks:** Weak independent-doctor demand in North America and a discretionary-spend slowdown.

**SOLV**
- **Q3 (reported Nov 5):** Sales fell 7% to $1.949B and organic sales fell 2.8%. About 630 basis points of that came from the reversal of Q2 orders placed ahead of the ERP cutover, which the company says is now complete. Adjusted EPS was $1.45, with a GAAP net loss of $12M.
- **Segments:** Organic growth by segment was Advanced Wound Care +7.2%, MedSurg -2.8%, Infection Prevention -5.7%, Dental -7.4%, and Health Information Systems +4.4%.
- **Guidance:** The adjusted EPS guide was raised to $7.20–7.30, and organic growth is expected toward the high end of 2.5–3.0%. Free cash flow of $200–300M was affirmed.
- **Stock reaction:** Shares rose roughly 4–5% after the report.
- **Catalysts:** The Health Information Systems unit is being separated or sold. No bidder or timing is public, and proceeds would go mainly to debt reduction. The company also has a $1B buyback program and an investor day in March 2027.
- **Debt:** Long-term debt is $4.56B. PFAS is a risk factor, with no amount disclosed.
- **Analysts:** Consensus is Hold, with August targets of $100–105 from Piper Sandler, Stifel, and Wedbush.

**COO (worst today, +0.0%)**
- **Q3 (early Sept):** Revenue was $1.066B, up 0.6%. Adjusted EPS was $1.15. The FY26 EPS guide was cut to $4.51–4.55 and the revenue guide to $4.229–4.252B. CooperVision is cutting US channel inventory, with Q4 organic growth guided at -2% to flat. CooperSurgical is guided at +4% to +6%.
- **Strategic review:** The board ended its review of selling CooperSurgical, saying the offers were inadequate. Shares fell about 14% to the mid-$50s, and the buyback authorization was raised to $3B.
- **Activism:** On Sept 18, Jana Partners (about 1.8% stake) demanded an external CEO search, a new board chair, and asset sales including CooperSurgical and possibly CooperVision. The Jana coverage mentions a possible proxy fight ahead of a January nomination deadline. A J.P. Morgan analyst cited by Reuters also named Browning West as an activist. I did not verify Browning West separately.
- **CEO exit:** On Oct 27, CEO Al White stepped down with immediate effect. Walt Rosebrough, former CEO of STERIS, is executive chair, and Russell Reynolds is running the CEO search. Nachman joins the board on Dec 8. FY26 guidance was reaffirmed, and shares fell about 3% after hours.

- **Next events:** The CEO announcement is open-ended. Q4 earnings are Dec 3 after the close (4:15 PM ET), and the Jana nomination deadline is in January.

**Networking equipment (CSCO, ANET, FFIV): research for the 2026-11-18 session**

The group's move today looks like a rebound in beaten-down names, not a new catalyst. The three stocks are in different places in their own cycles. No source ties the basket's move to one event.

**What the market did today**
- The Nasdaq closed up 0.42% at 24,430. The S&P 500 fell 0.24% to 7,323, below its 200-day average, and the Dow fell 1.11%. [Motley Fool via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-nov-18-230002098.html)

- Nvidia fell about 2.9%, reversing its post-earnings gain. Anthropic's IPO is pending.
- Tech was not broadly bid. The Technology Equipment industry fell 0.25% while ANET rose, so networking outperformed rather than rode a sector rally. [TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262311695-market-movers-anet-20261118)

**Cisco (CSCO), +2.2% today, the laggard and likely the below-50-day name**
- Fiscal Q1 2027 (reported Nov 12): revenue was $18.5B, up 24%, the fastest growth in over 15 years. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.40 against $1.33 expected. Networking product revenue rose 43%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/cisco-csco-q1-2027-earnings.html)
- Cisco doubled its hyperscaler AI infrastructure target to $9B for fiscal 2027. It raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8-75.8B and EPS guidance to $5.47-5.53.
- The stock fell anyway. Non-GAAP gross margin dropped 250 basis points to 65.6%, blamed on the AI hardware mix and memory costs, and the CFO guided full-year margin slightly below 65%. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-cisco-stock-falling-today-111503642.html)
- The fiscal Q2 revenue guide of $18.0-18.2B is below Q1. The CEO called hyperscaler demand "lumpy."
- Analysts split:
  - Citi cut its target to $120 from $139 (Buy kept), saying growth likely peaked in the October quarter.
  - Wells Fargo flagged product order growth decelerating.
  - Morgan Stanley downgraded on Nov 5 (target $120), warning of customers pulling purchases forward ahead of price increases.
  - Piper, Truist and Rosenblatt cut targets.
  - HSBC upgraded to Buy with a $133 target.
  - [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cisco-s-growth-may-have-peaked-despite-raised-ai-revenue-outlook-says-citi-barclays-sees-margins-holding-up/cNbRTvGR9fO), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/price-target/26/11/63251347/cisco-systems-posts-strong-q3-beat-analyst-cuts-price-target-despite-fastest-growth-in-over-15-years)

That is about 10% lower over the past month, but still up about 28% year to date. It was about $102 before earnings, and one source puts it at $96.34 on Nov 13.
- It trades at about 18x forward earnings, against 67x for Arista.

**Arista (ANET), the AI-networking leader, derated from its October high**
- Q3 (reported Nov 4): revenue was $3.66B, up 58.5%, and EPS was $1.20 against $1.08 expected. The first 2027 outlook is 38-40% growth, about $18.5B, against roughly $16.4B expected beforehand. [Investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-arista-networks-tops-q3-2026-estimates-shares-jump-93CH-4954192)
- The stock jumped on the print. Sources conflict on whether it held; one says up over 10% on Nov 4.
- Margin is the concern. Adjusted gross margin was 64% in Q3. Q4 is guided to 63-64% and fiscal 2027 to 62-64%. Supplier purchase commitments were $11.4B and inventory was $3.2B, both rising. [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/anet/articles/626190/what-could-derail-arista-networks-stock/2026-11-18)

- Nov 17 news: Arista launched Etherlink R4 routers and 800G optics for distributed inference at SC26. Availability is staggered, with one platform due in early 2027. The 60% power claim is a vendor claim, and roughly 30% of Arista's AI business is now "scale-across." [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/17/arista-takes-aim-at-the-next-ai-network-battleground-distributed-inference/)
- Risks named: customer concentration, competition from Cisco and Nvidia Spectrum-X, and insider sales. I found nothing showing today's +3.7% was driven by more than the product launch and an AI-infrastructure bounce.

**F5 (FFIV), +5.2% to $321.04, the best member and a bounce after a crash**
- Fiscal Q4 (reported Oct 27) beat: revenue was $917M, up 13%, and EPS was $4.42 against $4.26 expected. The stock then fell 15-20% on Oct 28, the worst day in over a decade by some accounts. [Investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-f5-tops-q4-2026-estimates-but-stock-slips-after-hours-93CH-4935711)

  - Legacy hardware refresh bookings expected to shrink in the second half.
  - Gross margin pressure from component costs.
  - Inventory build and supplier prepayments.

# Labs and clinical research (LH, DGX, IQV): research as of the 2026-11-18 close

## Bottom line
The 2.9% "gain" is mostly relative strength in a down day for health care, not a rally in these stocks. The sources I found put XLV down about 2% on Wednesday. Humana fell 12.98%, UnitedHealth 10.21%, Elevance 7.63% and Centene 7.03% after a CMS proposed rule on Medicare Advantage audits (Stock Titan; a market recap put health care at -2.2%). I did not find XLV's exact close. If it was about -2%, the basket's own move was roughly +0.9%. That is my inference from the figures you gave, not a sourced number. The MarketBeat intraday XLV prints I saw were about -1.4% to -2.0%.

No lab, diagnostics or CRO name appears in any coverage of today's move. I found no company-specific news for LH, DGX or IQV on 11/18.

The three names share a theme (Q3 beats and raised guidance) but have different risks. LH and DGX sit at or near all-time highs with a shared policy risk, the 2027 Medicare lab cuts under PAMA (the lab payment law). IQV has been a laggard with no stated cause.

## Labcorp (LH)
- **Q3 (reported 10/28):**
  - Revenue was $3.81B, up 6.9%. Adjusted EPS was $4.78, up 14.5%.
  - Full-year revenue growth guidance is now 5.9% to 6.7%. Adjusted EPS guidance is $18.30 to $18.70, up 18 cents at the midpoint.
  - Biopharma Laboratory Services revenue grew about 8.5%, with central labs up 11.5%. That unit's guidance midpoint was raised by 109 basis points.
  - One secondary source gives that unit's margin as 18.3%, up 180 basis points. I did not find this in Labcorp's own release.
- **Deals:**
  - It closed Millennium Health on 11/4. Other deals cited are MLM Medical Labs, BioReference assets (about $260M of first-year revenue) and Myriad's prenatal business. Sources disagree on how many are still pending.
  - Q3 acquisition spend was $255.5M.
- **Price:**
  - It hit an all-time high of about $374 around 11/12. A 11/16 insider sale was at about $372.58.
  - It is up about 49% year to date, at 30x earnings versus a five-year median of 25.6x. GuruFocus calls it about 30% above fair value.
- **Analysts:** Truist raised its target to $395, UBS to $420, and Mizuho to $400. HSBC upgraded to Buy.
- **Dates:**
  - The ex-dividend date is 11/24 ($0.72).
  - 2027 guidance comes in February.
- **Insiders:** EVP Amy Summy sold small amounts (365 shares on 11/16, about $136K).

## Quest (DGX)
- **Q3 (10/22):**
  - Revenue was $3.10B, up 10.0%, mostly organic. Adjusted EPS was $3.00, up 15.4%.
  - Full-year revenue guidance rose to $12.065B to $12.105B. Adjusted EPS guidance rose to $11.25 to $11.35 from $11.05 to $11.25.
  - One secondary source gives volumes up about 14.5% and revenue per requisition down 4.2%. It attributes the dip to the Fresenius and Corewell partnerships. This comes from one write-up, so check the 8-K.
- **Price:**
  - It made a 12-month high around 11/11. The CAO sold 11,776 shares on 11/13 at about $260.17 (about $3.06M).
  - Other insiders also sold. It is up about 50% year to date, and GuruFocus calls it overvalued against a fair value of $204.
- **Analysts:** Baird's target is $262 (Neutral), Barclays' is $260 (Overweight), and UBS's is $250 (Neutral).
- **Dates:**
  - Quest presented at Jefferies in London on 11/17. I found no coverage of what it said.
  - The CFO has a fireside chat at Evercore on 12/1.
  - Investor Day is 3/25/2027.
- **Other:** It paid a $13M kickback settlement.

## IQVIA (IQV)
- **Q3 (10/27):**
  - Revenue was $4.43B, up 8%, with organic growth about 6%. Adjusted EPS was $3.34, up 11.3%.
  - Guidance is $17.35B to $17.5B revenue, $4.025B to $4.055B adjusted EBITDA, and $12.90 to $13.00 adjusted EPS.
  - Net debt is $13.8B, or 3.45x leverage.
- **Demand:**
  - Net new bookings were $3.2B, up 15%. Book-to-bill was 1.2, which management called the strongest clinical bookings in four years. Trailing-twelve-month bookings were $11.7B.
  - Request-for-proposal flow and trial starts are up high single digits.
  - Emerging biopharma funding is $90B year to date, up more than 85%. Cancellations were within the historical range.
- **Watch item:** Backlog was cut about $2.1B for inactive trials, to $32.6B. Management says this has no effect on guidance, bookings or next-twelve-month revenue (about $9.4B, up 10%).
- **Risks:**
  - Management cited drug pricing pressure from the administration's most-favored-nation policy and tariffs as uncertainty.
  - Earlier 2026 sector coverage tied CRO weakness to fears that AI lets drugmakers bring trial work in-house.
- **Price:**
  - It fell six straight sessions through 11/17, down 7.6% to $257.60. That is 7.8% below its 52-week high of $279.36 and about 30x earnings.
  - Trefis found no company-specific cause for the slide. Against an S&P 500 down 2.7% over the same stretch, it called the move "mostly IQVIA's own story."
  - Today's +0.1% (your figure) probably ended the streak.
  - An insider (Sherbet) sold 4,446 shares on 11/9.
- **Dates:** Investor Day is 12/1 (9:00 AM to about 12:30 PM ET), and detailed 2027 guidance comes in February. I found no sell-side 2027 consensus.

## Shared catalyst: PAMA and the RESULTS Act
- CMS's preliminary 2027 lab rates (released 9/22) average about 16% cuts, with a 15% annual cap and about $1B in savings. They take effect 1/1/2027, with up to 15% more in each of 2028 and 2029.
- Final rates are expected in November. I did not find them published yet.
- Labcorp puts the 2027 impact at about $125M. Quest says about 1% of revenue. Evercore estimates $90M to $100M of operating income for Quest.
- The RESULTS Act would cap cuts at 5% and move rate-setting to a claims database. Industry wants it in a year-end spending package.
- The CBO score was due in November, and I did not find it. AdvaMed was still lobbying on 11/18.
- Congress has delayed these cuts six times, and TD Cowen thinks a delay is most likely. Both companies say they would offset part of any cut.

Two outcomes to plan for:
- A final-rate announcement or a legislative delay would hit LH and DGX in opposite ways. A delay is upside, and final rates matching the preliminary ones are mostly priced in.
- IQV is largely insulated from PAMA, so a lab-only move would split the basket.

## For the 1 to 10 session decision
- **Dated catalysts:**
  - 11/24: LH ex-dividend.
  - Any day: final CMS lab rates, the CBO score, and lame-duck spending-bill text.
  - 12/1: IQV Investor Day and the DGX Evercore chat.
- **The basket's relative strength is a one-day artifact** of the insurer selloff. If managed care rebounds, XLV catches up and the relative gain reverses without any change in the three stocks.
- **The signals are uneven.** LH and DGX are extended near highs and have taken insider selling, so there is limited valuation cushion. IQV has the strongest fundamental news (record bookings, funding rebound) but poor price action and no stated reason for it.
- **Treat the basket as three separate stories**, not one. IQV and the two labs trade on different drivers.

## Gaps
- I found no coverage of Jefferies commentary, today's closing prices for the three names, or short interest.
- Several figures come from single secondary sources. These are the Labcorp unit margin, Quest's volume and revenue-per-requisition numbers, and the Labcorp deal count and book-to-bill. Treat them as unconfirmed.

  - Felzartamab data in antibody-mediated rejection (AMR, a kidney-transplant problem) is expected in the first half of 2027.

  - I could not open the TheStreet article (HTTP 403), so the upgrade date and thesis come from a search snippet only.

Searches stopped surfacing new items by the end. This is what I found on GDS Holdings (GDS).

**The short version**
- The selloff looks driven by the sector and by sentiment. I found no GDS-specific bad news.
- Fundamentals were strong as of the August results.
- The next catalyst is the Q3 report on Nov 25, which falls inside the one-to-ten-session window. After the drop, it cuts both ways.

**Price action (aggregator data, figures vary by source)**
- GDS fell from about $22 on Nov 9 to $15.66 at the Nov 18 close. That is a drop of about 30% in seven sessions.
- Daily moves: roughly -12% on Nov 12, a gap down on Nov 16 (close $19.81, open $17.93, about -13.7% intraday), and about -8% on Nov 17. The Nov 17 close was $16.41, on 5.2M shares against a 2.2M average.
- On Nov 18 it hit an intraday low of about $15.37, which is the new 52-week low.
- The 50-day average is about $27.30 and the 200-day about $35.34. The stock is far below both.
- MarketBeat said large put volume traded on Nov 17. I could not open that page (HTTP 403), so I don't have the details.

**What I could and could not tie to the drop**
- MarketBeat, which I opened, cites no news for the drop. I found no downgrade, short report or company announcement.
- On Nov 16 the US Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips (TechCrunch, NPR and Al Jazeera all report it).
  - It requires a license to ship advanced AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere that may serve China-based customers.
  - It was issued days before the Trump-Xi APEC meeting and amid the Nvidia scandal.
  - No source I read names GDS or any other China data center operator as affected.
  - One Longbridge headline, which I couldn't open, links a GDS drop to chip transshipment controls. Treat that link as plausible but unconfirmed. Its date is also unclear, so it may be an earlier episode.
- Chinese ADRs and AI names were weak at the same time. One report says the Golden Dragon index fell more than 3% on Nov 12, and VNET fell about 9.6% in one report whose date I couldn't confirm.
- The GuruFocus note said GDS was down 38.6% year to date as of Nov 10.

**Business setup (Q2 report, Aug 13, from the SEC 6-K)**
- Revenue was RMB3.09B (US$455M), up 6.5%. Adjusted EBITDA was up 2.5%, with the margin down to 45.5% from 47.3% on utility costs.
- Utilization was 79.2%. Cash was RMB14.9B against total debt of about RMB46.1B.
- Guidance was raised: revenue RMB12.7–13.0B, adjusted EBITDA RMB5.9–6.1B, and a 2026 bookings target of 1GW (up from 500MW).
- First-half bookings were a record 470MW. Binding commitments are above 2GW. Management says all sales carry take-or-pay terms.
- Capex was raised to about RMB10B, funded roughly 60% by project debt and 40% by equity.
- Management guided to EBITDA acceleration from the second half of 2027, not before. Near-term growth is low, and the stock trades on the bookings story.
- Q2 net income of RMB838M was mostly a RMB960M dilution gain on DayOne, so it is not operating profit.
- Free cash flow is negative and leverage is high. A second asset injection into a C-REIT is under regulatory review, and the guidance excludes it.
- Analysts: consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target of about $48 (five analysts). Raymond James has a $51 target from September. These are stale relative to the price.

**DayOne (GDS's former international arm)**
- GDS holds a minority stake. Estimates range from about 24% to 35.6%, and a January sale left it holding about $2.2B at Series C pricing.
- In January GDS sold about $385M of shares back to DayOne.
- DayOne filed a public F-1 on Oct 5 for a Nasdaq listing as DODC. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, BofA, Citi and BNP are the banks.
- Earlier reports pointed to a $3–5B raise at roughly $20B. I found no price range or roadshow, so the timing is still open.
- First-half revenue was $512M, up from $151.5M, with a net loss of $77.2M.
- About 81.5–87% of revenue comes from Malaysia, and one customer is about 69%, reportedly ByteDance. This is a possible link to the new chip rule: offshore data centers serving Chinese customers are exactly its target. That is my inference, not something a source states.
- A DayOne pricing would be a positive catalyst for GDS. A delay or a weak valuation would hurt.

**Earnings, Nov 25**
- GDS confirmed it will report Q3 before the US open on Nov 25. The call is at 7:00 AM ET (6:00 AM CT).
- The key items to watch are bookings against the 1GW target, utilization, utility-cost margins, capex and financing, the C-REIT status, DayOne commentary, and any remarks on the chip rules.
- An earlier-dated aggregator report said earnings had been a source of selling in past quarters.

**For the 1–10 session decision**
- Bull case: oversold, with RSI 24 and a roughly 30% drop in seven sessions. Growth guidance and bookings are strong. Earnings on Nov 25 and a possible DayOne launch could reverse it.
- Bear case: the trend is broken, with a falling 50-day below the 200-day. The chip rule and APEC headlines are unresolved, and the cause of the drop is not confirmed. Leverage and negative free cash flow limit any bounce.
- Volatility is extreme, with ATR at 11.4% of price. A move in either direction can easily cross a stop.
- The earnings gap risk is real. Past quarters have seen drops of 5–16% on results, per Tiger Brokers headlines I could not open.

agents.report:
# Natera (NTRA): research for the 1-10 session decision

## Bottom line
NTRA is a fast-growing business that has been repriced hard. It had a strong operating quarter and a raised guide. The sell-off came from three things: a wider-than-expected loss, a big spending step-up, and a surprise CEO change. It was also priced at a stretched multiple going in, and that multiple has now compressed.

I found no new fundamental break since the November 5 report. Nothing I could find explains the extra leg down on November 16. The setup is an oversold bounce candidate in a healthy business. It has an overhang of "who is the new CEO and will spending pay off" and no scheduled catalyst I could confirm inside 10 sessions.

## Timeline
- **Oct 6-29:** The stock peaked, with a 52-week high of about $437 (Weiss). It closed at $436 on Oct 29. Several banks had raised targets in October, e.g. Barclays to $475 and Citi to $480 (Oct 7). The stock traded at about 17-20x sales, against a five-year average near 8.9x ([Yahoo/TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/natera-sinks-14-ceo-steve-143345879.html)).
- **Oct 30 and Nov 2:** The stock fell 5.0% on Oct 30. On Nov 2 it fell 8.5% with no company news. All five peers on Trefis's list fell (Myriad -7.9%, Guardant -4.5%). The S&P 500 was down 0.5% and the Nasdaq 1.1%. This looks like a group or momentum de-rating, and it has no confirmed cause ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/ntra/articles/622219/what-just-happened-to-natera-stock/2026-11-03)).
- **Nov 3:** Medicare, through MolDX, expanded Signatera coverage to serial surveillance in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) ([Nasdaq/BusinessWire](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/medicare-expands-coverage-signateratm-mrd-test-hepatocellular-carcinoma-2026-11-03)). The stock did not hold up on it.
- **Nov 5 (after the close), Q3 results ([8-K/press release](https://www.natera.com/company/news/natera-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results/)):**
  - Revenue was $794.0M, up 34.1%. Consensus was about $707-709M.
  - The GAAP loss was $0.42 per share against about $0.27-0.28 expected. The net loss was $59.9M, narrower than $87.5M a year ago.
  - Gross margin was 64.7%.
  - Oncology tests were about 339.5K, up 60.9%. Clinical MRD (minimal residual disease) volume was about 316K, up 56%.
  - Signatera's average selling price was about $1,290, up from $1,271 in Q2.
  - 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $3.005-3.035B from $2.85-2.91B.
  - SG&A guidance rose to $1.225-1.300B from $1.125-1.225B. R&D rose to $825-925M. That is about $113M more at the midpoints. The causes were one-time legal costs, pharma commercial investment, and faster MRD trial enrollment.
- **Nov 6:** The stock fell 14.6%, its largest one-day drop in a year, to about $303.50 from $363.76. Guardant reported the same evening: revenue up 36% to $361M, higher guidance, and higher spending.
- **Nov 16:** There was a further drop of 6-10%, depending on the source. Weiss says -6.37% to $298.77 from $319.09. GuruFocus says -9.6% to $288.48. Those are probably different snapshots. I found no company news that day. Finviz has a headline attributing it to a risk-off sell-off in diagnostics, but only one source says so. Quiver and Weiss call it continued post-earnings repricing.

## The story behind the numbers
**CEO change.** Steve Chapman, CEO for almost eight years, is stepping down. He said "now is an excellent time to transition." He stays on as a consultant and advisor. Solomon Moshkevich, previously president of clinical diagnostics, takes over. He helped launch Signatera and Prospera. He said he shaped most prior strategy and expects no radical change ([call summary, automated transcript](https://gloom.sh/stocks/ntra/transcripts/q3-2026)). I found no stated reason for the timing beyond "from a position of strength."

**2029 target.** Management targets about $6B of revenue, roughly double 2026. The plan assumes a Signatera average selling price of about $1,450 (management said it could reach $2,000+ longer term), plus Japan and pharma/data licensing. Pharma and data licensing is expected to add several hundred million dollars. Early cancer screening is expected to be a small contributor in 2028-29. The CFO called the target aggressive but achievable.

**Cash and profitability.** The company generated free cash flow in Q3. The CFO expects another positive quarter and improving EBITDA in Q4. Early-detection spend is over $100M with no revenue yet. The CFO said R&D could be cut 70% or more without hurting the core business, but management chose to keep investing. 2027 operating expense growth is guided to 10-12%.

**Margins.** The 2026 gross margin range is 64-66%. Newer products (Signatera Genome, Fetal Focus) will pressure cost of goods near term. Management targets 70%+ long term. The CFO also said average selling prices won't necessarily rise steadily. For 2027 planning he used flat prices as the base case.

**Reimbursement.** Natera has submitted 11 dossiers to MolDX, one per tumor type, and liver is approved. About 10 are pending, and management won't predict timing. One analyst estimate puts the potential average selling price uplift at $150-200 over 12-18 months. This is real upside, but the timing is unpredictable.

## Competition
- **Guardant (Reveal):** Growing about as fast. It is burning up to $220M of free cash flow this year. One source says its tumor-informed Reveal Ultra is targeting a 2026 launch against Signatera.
- **Exact Sciences:** Its Oncodetect holds Medicare coverage for colorectal cancer, stages II-IV. One blog mentions a 22% drop in Exact after its Q3 report, but it was undated, so I can't confirm it.
